nodes.label: Create an account
nodes.description:
**As a** new user, **I want** to register an account on my 4ga Boards instance, **so that** I can sign in and use it.

**Steps**
1. Open the web address of your 4ga Boards instance.
2. On the login screen click **Create an account**.
3. Enter **Email** and **Password** (choose a strong one).
4. Tick the checkbox to **Accept** the **Terms of Service** and **Privacy Policy**.
5. Click **Register**.

**Expected**: Your account is created. Errors shown for a weak password, an email already in use, or policy not accepted. A **Back to login page** button (after "Already a user?") returns to login.

**Preconditions**: the instance has registration (local registration) enabled; otherwise the form shows "registration disabled" and an administrator must add you manually.

nodes.label: Sign in with an SSO provider
nodes.description:
**As a** new user, **I want** to register with my SSO provider, **so that** I need no separate password.

**Steps**
1. Open the instance and click **Create an account** on the login screen.
2. Under the **or** separator click **Continue with Google**, **Microsoft**, **GitHub** or **OIDC** (a generic OIDC provider may show its own named button).
3. Authenticate at the provider.

**Expected**: Account is created and you are signed in; the display name defaults to the part of the email before "@". Errors: SSO registration disabled, no OIDC profile found, domain not allowed.

**Preconditions**: the administrator enabled SSO sign-in for at least one provider. Docs list Google, Microsoft, GitHub and generic OIDC; the app shows the same four buttons.

nodes.label: Log in with username or email and password
nodes.description:
**As a** registered user, **I want** to log in with my username or email and password, **so that** I can reach my boards.

**Steps**
1. Open the instance address; the **Log in** screen appears.
2. Enter **Email or username** and **Password**.
3. Click **Log in**.

**Expected**: You are signed in and taken into the app. If SSO is configured, **Continue with <provider>** buttons appear below an **or** separator as an alternative. Failed attempts show an error message. A **New to 4ga Boards?** link offers **Create an account**.

**Preconditions**: you have an account. Not described in the docs (docs only cover registration).

nodes.label: Log out
nodes.description:
**As a** signed-in user, **I want** to log out, **so that** nobody else can use my session on this device.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar / user menu in the header (popup lists Profile, Preferences, Account, Authentication, About).
2. Click **Log Out** at the bottom of the popup.

**Expected**: Your session ends and the login screen is shown. The button is disabled while logging out.

**Preconditions**: signed in. Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Try the demo instance
nodes.description:
**As a** prospective user, **I want** to try 4ga Boards in the public demo instance, **so that** I can evaluate it without installing anything.

**Steps**
1. Open the demo instance at demo.4gaboards.com (docs link).
2. Click **Create an account** and register as usual.

**Expected**: In demo mode the header shows banners "Star 4ga Boards on GitHub!" and "We'd love to hear your feedback!". Settings pages show "Demo Mode - some features affecting other users are disabled! Every new user receives admin privileges." Limitations are listed on the "Try 4ga Boards" page on 4gaboards.com.

**Preconditions**: instance runs with demo mode enabled (DEMO_MODE=true).

nodes.label: Change my avatar
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to set or remove my profile picture, **so that** others recognise me.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Profile** (Settings > Profile).
2. Next to **Profile picture** click the avatar or **Edit**.
3. In the popup click **Upload new avatar** and choose an image file from disk (any image type), or click **Delete avatar** to remove the current one.

**Expected**: The new avatar replaces the old one (or the initials fallback is shown after deleting). The avatar appears disabled while updating.

**Preconditions**: signed in. Docs say the avatar is added "from the disc"; **Delete avatar** appears only when an avatar exists.

nodes.label: Edit my profile
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to edit my profile details, **so that** my displayed name, phone and organization are correct.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Profile**.
2. Edit **Name**, **Phone** and **Organization**.
3. Click **Save**.

**Expected**: The new values are stored and the displayed name changes across the app. **Save** stays disabled until something has changed.

**Preconditions**: signed in. Docs mention remembering to click Save.

nodes.label: Change my username or email
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to change my username or email address, **so that** my login identity stays current.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Account** (Settings > Account).
2. The page shows "Username: ..." and "Email: ... (verified / not verified)".
3. Click **Edit Username** (or **Edit Email**).
4. Enter **New username** (or **New email**) and your **Current password**.
5. Click **Save**.

**Expected**: The value is updated in the Account page. A changed email must be verified again.

**Preconditions**: signed in. The current password is requested only for password-authenticated accounts (SSO users are not asked), which the docs do not say: docs state the password is always required.

nodes.label: Change my password
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to change my password, **so that** I can keep my account secure.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Authentication** (Settings > Authentication).
2. Click **Edit Password**.
3. Enter **Current password** and **New password**.
4. Click **Save**.

**Expected**: The password is updated; a weak or wrong current password shows an error (e.g. "Invalid current password").

**Preconditions**: signed in. For SSO-only accounts the button reads **Set Password** and no current password is asked (not in the docs).

nodes.label: Verify my email address
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to verify my email address by clicking the link I receive, **so that** I can get email notifications.

**Steps**
1. Receive the verification email sent by the instance.
2. Click the link in the email.
3. You are redirected to Settings > Account.

**Expected**: A popup says "Email Verified Successfully"; on failure it says "Email Verification Failed", "Please try again!" and a "Reason: ...". The Account page then shows your email as "(verified)".

**Preconditions**: a mail/notifications service is available. Docs: email notifications are only sent to verified users.

nodes.label: Resend the verification email
nodes.description:
**As a** user with an unverified email, **I want** to resend the verification email, **so that** I can complete verification if I missed or lost the first one.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Account**.
2. Click **Resend Verification Email**.

**Expected**: A new email is sent and the button is disabled with a countdown (about 60 seconds, shown as mm:ss) before it can be used again.

**Preconditions**: the mail service is available (button hidden otherwise). Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Generate an API client
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to generate an API client, **so that** scripts can authenticate on my behalf.

**Steps**
1. Open the user menu and click **Authentication**.
2. Click **Generate API Client**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose **Permissions**: **all**, a group (e.g. attachments), or single permissions (e.g. attachments.create); at least one is required.
4. Click **Generate**.

**Expected**: A step shows the **Client Id** and **API Client Secret** with the note "Please copy and save the API Client Secret. It will be visible only during this session." The client appears under **API Clients [n]** with created/last-used dates ("Never" if unused) and its permissions ("all" for *).

**Preconditions**: signed in. Docs: any user can generate one; permissions use `*`, `group.*` or `group.action`.

nodes.label: Edit an API client and limit its permissions
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to edit an API client and limit its permissions, **so that** a script has only the access it needs.

**Steps**
1. Open **Authentication** from the user menu.
2. In the **API Clients** list click the pencil icon (**Edit API Client**) of a client.
3. Change the **Name** and tick or untick **Permissions** (all, groups, single permissions).
4. Click **Save**.

**Expected**: The list shows the updated name and permissions. At least one permission must stay selected ("Please select at least one permission").

**Preconditions**: an API client exists.

nodes.label: Copy an API client id or secret
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to copy an API client's id or secret, **so that** I can paste it into my script.

**Steps**
1. Open **Authentication** from the user menu.
2. In a client's entry click the copy icon next to **Client Id** (**Copy Client Id**) or **Client Secret** (**Copy Client Secret**).

**Expected**: The value is copied to the clipboard.

**Preconditions**: an API client exists. The secret row is shown only when the secret is available in the client. Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Regenerate an API client secret
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to regenerate an API client's secret, **so that** a leaked secret stops working.

**Steps**
1. Open **Authentication** from the user menu.
2. Click the reset icon (**Reset API Client**) on the client; alternatively in **Edit API Client** tick **Regenerate Secret** and click **Save**.

**Expected**: A new secret is shown with the note that it is visible only during this session; the old secret no longer works.

**Preconditions**: an API client exists. Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Delete an API client
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to delete an API client, **so that** its credentials can no longer be used.

**Steps**
1. Open **Authentication** from the user menu.
2. Click the trash icon (**Delete API Client**) on the client.
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this API client?" by clicking **Delete API Client**.

**Expected**: The client disappears from the list and the count in **API Clients [n]** drops ("No API Clients" when empty).

**Preconditions**: an API client exists. Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Create a card through the API
nodes.description:
**As a** developer, **I want** to create a card by calling the API with my client credentials, **so that** I can automate card creation.

**Steps**
1. In **Authentication** generate an API client with the `cards.create` permission and note its Client Id and Secret.
2. Fetch the target `listId` with another API call (or from the browser inspector).
3. Send `POST <server-url>/api/lists/<listId>/cards` with headers `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Client-Id: <client id>`, `X-Client-Secret: <client secret>` and body `{"name": "Card Name"}`.

**Expected**: A card named "Card Name" is created in that list.

**Preconditions**: API client with cards.create. Server reads the X-Client-Id header (server/api/policies/is-authenticated.js). Docs-only: no UI in the client for this.

nodes.label: Browse projects on the dashboard
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to see all my projects on the dashboard, **so that** I can jump into any of them.

**Steps**
1. Click the 4ga Boards logo in the header (or open the app root).
2. Look at the project tiles.

**Expected**: The header reads "Showing N Projects [M Boards]". Each project is a tile showing its name, with a notification count badge if it has unread notifications and its background gradient or image. Clicking a tile opens that project (its boards). With no projects you see "No Projects Available - Ask for an invitation." (or an Add Project button if you may create projects).

**Preconditions**: You belong to at least one project.

nodes.label: Filter projects on the dashboard
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to type part of a project name in the sidebar filter while on the dashboard, **so that** only matching projects stay on the dashboard.

**Steps**
1. Open the dashboard.
2. Click the "Filter projects..." field at the top of the sidebar (filter type shows P).
3. Type part of a name; matching works on any part of the name.

**Expected**: Dashboard tiles and the sidebar narrow to matches, the dashboard header reads "Showing X of N projects", and a counter appears under the field. Clearing the field restores all tiles. Opening the dashboard resets the filter type to projects.

**Docs vs app**: Docs only describe the sidebar filter; the dashboard filtering is app behaviour (Filter.jsx and Projects.jsx).

nodes.label: Create a project
nodes.description:
**As a** admin, **I want** to create a project, **so that** I have a container for related boards.

**Steps**
1. Click "+ Add Project" at the bottom of the sidebar or at the top right of the dashboard.
2. In the popup "Add Project", type a name in "Enter project name...".
3. Press Enter or click the "Add Project" button.

**Expected**: The popup closes and the new project appears as a tile on the dashboard and in the sidebar. An empty name is rejected: the field is focused and shown in error.

**Preconditions**: You are an admin, or the instance setting "Project Creation For All Users" is on.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say only administrators see the option; the app also shows it to everyone when project creation for all users is enabled.

nodes.label: Rename a project
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to rename a project, **so that** its name stays accurate.

**Steps**
1. Hover the project name in the sidebar (or a dashboard tile) and click the ellipsis button ("Edit Project"), or right-click it if "Open context menu on right-click" is on.
2. Click "Rename Project".
3. Edit the name and save (Enter).
4. Alternative: open Project Settings, change the name field and click "Save".

**Expected**: The project shows the new name in the sidebar, dashboard tile and project settings.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Reorder projects
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to drag projects into a different order in the sidebar, **so that** the ones I use most are on top.

**Steps**
1. Hover a project row in the sidebar to reveal the two-arrow handle ("Reorder projects").
2. Press and hold the handle and drag the project above or below another project (or below the last one).
3. Release.

**Expected**: A placeholder shows the drop position; after the drop the sidebar keeps the new order.

nodes.label: Delete a project
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to delete a project, **so that** an obsolete project and its boards are removed.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings (cog icon next to "+ Add Board", or ellipsis menu > "Project Settings").
2. In the "Danger Zone" click "Delete Project".
3. In the confirmation popup ("Are you sure you want to delete this project?") click "Delete project".

**Expected**: The project is removed from the dashboard and sidebar.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Open project settings
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to open the settings of a project I manage, **so that** I can change its name, managers and background.

**Steps**
1. On the project's board view click the "Project Settings" cog icon in the top-right toolbar, or hover the project in the sidebar, click the ellipsis and choose "Project Settings".
2. To leave, click the arrow icon ("Back to Project") or the 4ga Boards logo (dashboard).

**Expected**: A "Project Settings" page opens with the project name, a name field with "Save", the "Managers" list, "Background" options and the "Danger Zone".

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Add or remove project managers
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to add or remove project managers, **so that** responsibility for a project can be shared or handed over.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings.
2. In "Managers" click the add-user icon ("Add Manager"), search users in "Search users..." and click a user to add them.
3. To remove: click a manager's avatar, then "Remove from project" and confirm "Remove manager".

**Expected**: The manager avatars update. The last manager cannot leave the project.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Leave a project
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to leave a project I manage, **so that** I am no longer responsible for it.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings.
2. In "Managers" click your own avatar.
3. Click "Leave project" and confirm in the popup ("Are you sure you want to leave the project?").

**Expected**: You are removed from the project's managers and it leaves your list. The "Leave project" button is not offered when you are the only manager.

**Preconditions**: You are a manager and not the only one.

nodes.label: Set a project background
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to pick a gradient background, **so that** the project is recognisable on the dashboard and as the backdrop.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings.
2. In "Background" click one of the gradient swatches.

**Expected**: The chosen swatch is highlighted; the project tile and the project's boards show that gradient.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Upload a project background image
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to upload my own image as the project background, **so that** the project uses a custom picture.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings > "Background".
2. Click "Upload New Image" and choose an image file.
3. If it is not already selected, click the image thumbnail.

**Expected**: A thumbnail appears; the selected one shows a star. The tile and the boards use the image as cover background.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

**Docs vs app**: Docs: "set the background image (with possibility to upload your own)". The app also offers "Delete Image" for the uploaded image.

nodes.label: Remove a project background
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to remove the background, **so that** the project returns to the plain look.

**Steps**
1. Open Project Settings > "Background".
2. Click "Remove Background" (shown only while a background is set).
3. To drop the uploaded file itself click "Delete Image".

**Expected**: The gradient or image disappears from the tile and boards.

**Preconditions**: A background is set.

nodes.label: Check project activity
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to see when a project was created and last updated and its recent activity, **so that** I can follow what changed.

**Steps**
1. Hover the project in the sidebar (or on the dashboard) and click the ellipsis ("Edit Project").
2. Click "Check Activity".

**Expected**: A popup titled "Activity for <project name>" shows created and updated times with who did it, followed by the activity list, loaded as you scroll.

nodes.label: Import the Getting Started project
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to import the Getting Started project, **so that** I get an interactive introduction to 4ga Boards.

**Steps**
1. Open Settings (user menu in the header).
2. Choose "About" in the settings sidebar.
3. Click "Import Getting Started Project".

**Expected**: A Getting Started project with its boards is created (in your interface language if available, English otherwise) and appears in the sidebar and dashboard. The button is disabled after one click.

nodes.label: Show or hide the sidebar
source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to hide and show the sidebar, **so that** the board gets more room.

**Steps**
1. Click the bar-and-arrow icon in the top-left, left of the logo (tooltip "Hide Sidebar" / "Show Sidebar").

**Expected**: The sidebar collapses or reappears. Width can be made narrower with "Compact Sidebar" in personal Preferences.

nodes.label: Filter the sidebar by project or board
source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to filter the sidebar by project or board name, **so that** I find a project or board quickly.

**Steps**
1. Click the filter field at the top of the sidebar ("Filter projects..." or "Filter boards...").
2. Type any part of a name.
3. Press Enter or just keep typing.

**Expected**: The tree narrows to matches, even for text in the middle of the name, and a counter such as "2 of 5 projects" shows. When filtering boards, matching boards stay visible inside collapsed projects.

nodes.label: Switch the sidebar filter type
source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to switch the sidebar filter between projects and boards, **so that** I search the right kind of item.

**Steps**
1. Click the two-arrow icon with a letter (P or B; tooltip "Toggle filter: boards/projects [Tab]"), or press Tab while typing in the filter.

**Expected**: The letter and placeholder change between P / "Filter projects..." and B / "Filter boards..." and the current text is applied to the new type. Opening a project switches to boards, the dashboard switches back to projects.

nodes.label: Clear the sidebar filter
nodes.source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to clear the sidebar filter, **so that** I see everything again.

**Steps**
1. With text in the filter click the "x" icon ("Clear filter"); in the app Escape in the field does the same.

**Expected**: The field empties and all projects and boards return; the current item is scrolled into view.

**Preconditions**: A filter is active.

nodes.label: Expand or collapse a project in the sidebar
source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to expand or collapse a project in the sidebar, **so that** I see its boards only when I need them.

**Steps**
1. Click the triangle left of the project name (tooltips "Show boards" / "Hide boards").

**Expected**: The boards you can access in that project are shown or hidden. The state is saved per user. The current project and active board filtering always show boards.

nodes.label: Navigate to a project or board from the sidebar
nodes.source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to click a project or board name in the sidebar, **so that** I jump to it.

**Steps**
1. Click a project name to open the project or a board name to open that board.

**Expected**: The page switches and the selected project or board is highlighted in the sidebar (blueish in docs).

nodes.label: Edit a project or board from the sidebar
nodes.source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to edit a project or board from the sidebar, **so that** I do not have to open it first.

**Steps**
1. Hover the project or board name and click the three-dot (ellipsis) button, or right-click if enabled in Preferences.
2. Project menu: "Rename Project", "Project Settings", "Check Activity", "Add Board".
3. Board menu: "Rename Board", "Edit GitHub Connection", "Export Board", "Check Activity", hide completed lists, "Email Card to Board", "Convert to Template", "Delete Board".

**Expected**: The matching popup or sub-step opens beside the sidebar. Rename/settings/delete entries show only to managers; "Check Activity" to everyone.

**Docs vs app**: Docs mention only a three-dot menu; menu entries are taken from ProjectActionsPopup and BoardActionsPopup.

nodes.label: Add a project or board from the sidebar
source: sidebar.md#Some actions you can perform within sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to add a project or board with the buttons at the bottom of the sidebar, **so that** I can create them without leaving the page.

**Steps**
1. Click "+ Add Project" (if allowed) or "+ Add Board" at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. For a board choose the project in the "Project" dropdown (preselected with the current project), type a name, pick a template and click "Add Board".

**Expected**: A new project or board appears in the sidebar.

**Preconditions**: "+ Add Board" shows only if you manage at least one project; "+ Add Project" only if you are an admin or project creation is open to all.

nodes.label: Create a board
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to create a board in a project, **so that** I can organise work in lists and cards.

**Steps**
1. Click "+ Add Board" (top right of a project, project ellipsis menu > "Add Board", or bottom of the sidebar).
2. Type the name in "Enter board name...".
3. Choose a project if the dropdown is shown; leave template as Empty.
4. Click "Add Board".

**Expected**: The board is created in the project and listed in the sidebar. Empty template gives a single "Done" list. Missing name or project marks the field in error.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Create a board from a template
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to start a board from a template, **so that** its lists and labels are prefilled.

**Steps**
1. Open the "Add Board" popup.
2. Enter a name and project.
3. In "Template" open the dropdown and choose a template (searchable).
4. Click "Add Board".

**Expected**: The board is created with the template's lists and labels, e.g. Simple: Open, Todo, In Progress, Done; Kanban adds To Test.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

**Docs vs app**: Docs list two templates (simple, kanban); the app has Empty, Simple, Kanban, Software Development and user/global templates.

nodes.label: Import a board from a 4ga Boards export
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to import a board from a 4ga Boards export, **so that** I can move boards between instances or users.

**Steps**
1. Open "Add Board".
2. Click "Import" and choose "From 4ga Boards"; select a .tgz file.
3. Enter the board name and pick the project.
4. Optionally tick the user checkboxes.
5. Click "Import Board".

**Expected**: The button shows the file name; the template picker is hidden. A new board with the exported content is created.

**Preconditions**: You hold a .tgz export; you manage the target project.

**Docs vs app**: board.md says import of 4ga Boards data uses .csv; import-export.md and the app (accept=".tgz") use .tgz.

nodes.label: Add project managers when importing a board
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to add the exported board's project managers on import, **so that** they keep their role.

**Steps**
1. Start importing a 4ga Boards .tgz file.
2. Tick the checkbox "Add project managers".
3. Click "Import Board".

**Expected**: Users who were project managers in the exported board are added as managers of the target project.

**Preconditions**: A 4ga Boards file is selected.

nodes.label: Create accounts for missing users when importing a board
nodes.description:
**As a** admin, **I want** to create accounts for users that don't exist yet, **so that** imported members aren't lost.

**Steps**
1. Start importing a 4ga Boards .tgz file.
2. Tick "Create accounts for non-existing users" (disabled with "(requires admin rights)" for non-admins).
3. Click "Import Board".

**Expected**: Accounts are created for exported members absent from this instance and they become board members.

**Preconditions**: A 4ga Boards file is selected; you are an admin.

nodes.label: Import a board from Trello
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to import a Trello board, **so that** I can migrate from Trello.

**Steps**
1. Export the Trello board as .json.
2. In "Add Board" click "Import" > "From Trello" and choose the .json file.
3. Enter the board name and choose the project.
4. Click "Import Board".

**Expected**: A working board is created including labels.

**Preconditions**: You manage the target project.

nodes.label: Export a board
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to export a board, **so that** I have a backup or can import it elsewhere.

**Steps**
1. Hover the board in the sidebar and click the ellipsis, or use the board toolbar ellipsis.
2. Click "Export Board".
3. Set the skip options if desired and click "Export Board".

**Expected**: A message says the download starts automatically when the export is ready, then closes after 5 seconds; a .tgz file is saved.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

**Docs vs app**: board.md says .csv; import-export.md and the app use .tgz.

nodes.label: Skip parts of a board when exporting
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to leave out parts of a board from an export, **so that** the file is smaller or private.

**Steps**
1. Open "Export Board".
2. Tick any of: "Skip attachments", "Skip user avatars", "Skip project backgrounds", "Skip metadata", "Skip actions (history)" (ticked by default).
3. Click "Export Board".

**Expected**: The exported file omits the ticked parts.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Rename a board
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to rename a board, **so that** its name stays accurate.

**Steps**
1. Hover the board in the sidebar, click the ellipsis, choose "Rename Board".
2. Type the new name and confirm.

**Expected**: The board name changes in the sidebar and toolbar.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Delete a board
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to delete a board, **so that** unused boards are removed.

**Steps**
1. Open the board ellipsis menu.
2. Click "Delete Board".
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this board?" with "Delete Board".

**Expected**: The board and its content disappear from the sidebar.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Reorder boards within a project
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to drag boards into a different order within a project, **so that** the order suits my workflow.

**Steps**
1. Hover a board in the sidebar and press and hold the two-arrow handle ("Reorder boards within the project")
2. Drag it above or below another board of the same project and release.

**Expected**: The sidebar keeps the new order; boards cannot be dragged to another project.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Leave a board
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to leave a board, **so that** I no longer see or get its notifications.

**Steps**
1. Open the board.
2. In the toolbar click your own avatar.
3. Click "Leave board" and confirm.

**Expected**: You are removed from the board and it disappears from your sidebar. The button is not offered if you are the last member.

**Preconditions**: You are a board member.

nodes.label: Check board activity
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to see a board's created/updated info and its activity, **so that** I can follow changes.

**Steps**
1. Open the board ellipsis menu (sidebar or toolbar).
2. Click "Check Activity".

**Expected**: A popup "Activity for <board name>" shows who created and last updated it and a scrollable activity list.

nodes.label: Subscribe to or unsubscribe from a board
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to subscribe to or unsubscribe from a board, **so that** I get notifications only for boards I care about.

**Steps**
1. Open the board.
2. Click the bell icon at the left of the toolbar (tooltip "Subscribe" or "Unsubscribe").

**Expected**: The icon toggles between a filled and empty bell and notifications follow the setting.

**Preconditions**: You are a board member.

nodes.label: Connect a board to a GitHub repository
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to link a board to a GitHub repository, **so that** the board can reference that repo.

**Steps**
1. Click the GitHub icon in the board toolbar (grey = "Not connected to GitHub").
2. In "Connect to GitHub" enter "Owner/Repo" in the field.
3. Click "Save" (or "Cancel").

**Expected**: The icon turns green with the tooltip "Connected to GitHub: <repo>" and a GitHub icon appears next to the board in the sidebar. An invalid name leaves the field in error.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

**Docs vs app**: The popup is labelled "[Not fully implemented]" in the app.

nodes.label: Edit a board's GitHub connection
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to change or remove the repository of a board, **so that** the link stays correct.

**Steps**
1. Click the green GitHub icon in the toolbar or next to the board in the sidebar (or ellipsis > "Edit GitHub Connection").
2. Change the repository, or clear the field.
3. Click "Save".

**Expected**: The new repo shows in the tooltip; an empty field disconnects it (icon grey).

**Preconditions**: A repository is already connected; you manage the project.

nodes.label: Convert a board to a template
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to turn a board into a template, **so that** new boards can reuse its lists and labels.

**Steps**
1. Open the board ellipsis menu.
2. Click "Convert to Template".
3. Edit the name in "Enter template name..." and confirm.

**Expected**: The template is saved and the Board Templates manager opens; it appears in the "Template" dropdown when adding boards.

**Preconditions**: You can edit the board or manage the project.

nodes.label: Manage board templates
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to open the board templates manager, **so that** I can review and maintain templates.

**Steps**
1. In the "Add Board" popup click the gear next to "Template" ("Manage Templates"), or use the board menu after "Convert to Template".

**Expected**: A "Board Templates" list shows each template with its lists and labels; global ones have a star and "Global" badge. Per row: toggle global (admin), rename, delete.

nodes.label: Rename a board template
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to rename a template, **so that** its name is clear.

**Steps**
1. Open "Board Templates".
2. Click the pencil ("Rename Template") on a row.
3. Edit the name, confirm.

**Expected**: The row shows the new name.

**Preconditions**: The template is your own, or you are an admin for global ones.

nodes.label: Delete a board template
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to delete a template, **so that** unused ones disappear.

**Steps**
1. Open "Board Templates".
2. Click the trash icon ("Delete Template") on a row.
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this template?" with "Delete".

**Expected**: The template is removed; with none left "No templates" is shown.

**Preconditions**: The template is your own, or you are an admin for global ones.

nodes.label: Filter board templates
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to filter the templates by name, **so that** I find one in a long list.

**Steps**
1. Open "Board Templates".
2. Type in "Filter templates...".

**Expected**: Only templates whose name contains the text (case-insensitive) stay visible.

nodes.label: Add a board member
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to add a member to a board, **so that** they can work on it.

**Steps**
1. Click the add-user icon ("Add User") in the board toolbar.
2. Search in "Search users..." and click a user.
3. Choose the permission (Editor or Viewer, optionally "Can comment")and click "Add Member".

**Expected**: The user's avatar appears in the toolbar.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Remove a board member
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to remove a member from a board, **so that** they lose access.

**Steps**
1. Click the member's avatar in the toolbar.
2. Click "Remove from board".
3. Confirm with "Remove member".

**Expected**: The avatar disappears and the user no longer sees the board.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

nodes.label: Set a board member's permissions
nodes.description:
**As a** project manager, **I want** to change a member's permissions, **so that** their access fits their role.

**Steps**
1. Click the member's avatar in the toolbar.
2. Click "Edit permissions".
3. Choose "Editor" (can edit the content of the board) or "Viewer" (can only view); for Viewer optionally tick "Can comment".
4. Click "Save".

**Expected**: The role badge on the member updates.

**Preconditions**: You manage the project.

**Docs vs app**: Docs list four roles (Project manager, Editor, Commenter, Viewer); the app dialog offers Editor and Viewer with a "Can comment" option, and project managers are set per project.

nodes.label: Keep working offline and save when the connection returns
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to be told when the connection is lost, **so that** changes aren't silently lost.

**Steps**
1. Lose the network or stop the server while the app is open.

**Expected**: A notice "No connection - Please don't reload the tab!" appears with "All changes will be saved automatically once the connection is restored"; clicking it collapses it, and it disappears when the socket reconnects.

**Docs vs app**: Only the notice and a serialized request queue exist in the client; true offline buffering was not verified from code.

nodes.label: Switch between board view and list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to switch a board between board view and list view **so that** I can see the same cards as columns or as a to-do table.

**Steps**
1. Open a board.
2. In the board toolbar (right side, before the project settings and board menu buttons) click the board icon ("Switch to Board View") or the list icon ("Switch to List View").

**Expected**: The board area shows either the kanban lists or the card table; the active icon is highlighted and the view is kept in the page path, so a card opened from it stays in the same view.

**Preconditions**: A board is open.

nodes.label: Choose the default board view
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to choose whether boards open in board view or list view **so that** every board opens the way I prefer.

**Steps**
1. Open your user settings and go to Preferences.
2. Find "Default View" and pick "List" or "Board" from the dropdown.

**Expected**: Boards you open afterwards start in the chosen view (unless the page path already names a view).

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

**Docs vs app**: Docs describe "board view or list view"; the app dropdown labels are "List" and "Board".

nodes.label: Use the kanban board view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to work on the board as kanban lists with cards **so that** I can see workflow stages as columns.

**Steps**
1. Open a board with "Board" selected in the toolbar view switch (click "Switch to Board View" if needed).
2. Add, drag and open cards in the lists.

**Expected**: Lists are shown side by side as columns holding their cards; the lower area scrolls horizontally when lists do not fit.

**Preconditions**: A board is open.

nodes.label: Use the list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see all cards of the board as a table, one card per row **so that** I can scan, sort and edit my tasks like a to-do list.

**Steps**
1. Open a board and click "Switch to List View" in the toolbar (or set "Default View" to "List" in Preferences).
2. Read the columns: notifications bell, done, name, labels, members, list, has-description tick, attachment count, comment count, due date, earliest due date, timer, tasks, and the card ellipsis menu.

**Expected**: A table with a header row, one row per card (after any active filters), and a bottom pane with pagination, a settings cog and Add List / Add Card buttons.

**Preconditions**: A board is open.

**Docs vs app**: Docs list 13 columns; the app also has a "Done" check column (shown by default) and optional hidden columns: cover image, created at/by, updated at/by, description.

nodes.label: Keep board and list views in sync
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** changes made in either view to appear in the other **so that** I never have to repeat work.

**Steps**
1. Change something in list view, e.g. edit a card name, move a card to another list, add a card or list.
2. Click "Switch to Board View" (or the reverse).

**Expected**: The same data is shown in both views, because both read the same board state. Sorting in list view does not reorder lists or cards in board view.

**Preconditions**: A board with cards.

nodes.label: Scroll the board horizontally
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to scroll across lists that do not fit on screen **so that** I can reach every list on a wide board.

**Steps**
1. In board view, hold Shift and use the mouse wheel over the board, or drag the scrollbar at the bottom.

**Expected**: The board scrolls sideways to reveal further lists.

**Preconditions**: Board view with more lists than fit the window.

**Docs vs app**: Shift+Scroll is documented (also in Useful Shortcuts); the app has no key handler for it, it relies on the horizontally scrollable board wrapper.

nodes.label: Scroll the board by dragging empty space
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to drag the board background to scroll it **so that** I can move around with the mouse only.

**Steps**
1. In board view, press the mouse button on an empty space of the board (the cursor becomes a hand).
2. Drag left or right.

**Expected**: The board scrolls horizontally following the mouse; text selection is suppressed during the drag.

**Preconditions**: Board view with more lists than fit the window.

nodes.label: Scroll through a list's cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to scroll the cards inside a long list **so that** I can see every card in it.

**Steps**
1. In board view, hover over a list full of cards.
2. Use the mouse wheel or the scrollbar at the right of the list.

**Expected**: The cards of that list scroll vertically while the other lists stay still.

**Preconditions**: A list with more cards than fit.

nodes.label: Hide or show completed lists
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to hide the lists marked as done from the board **so that** my board shows only open work.

**Steps**
1. Open the board menu with the vertical ellipsis button at the right end of the toolbar ("Edit Board").
2. Click "Hide Completed Lists" (it reads "Show Completed Lists" once hidden).

**Expected**: Lists marked as done ("Mark as Done" in the list menu) disappear from the board, and reappear after "Show Completed Lists". The choice is stored per board membership, so it affects only you.

**Preconditions**: A board with at least one list marked as done.

**Docs vs app**: Not described in the docs, which only cover the per-list collapse triangle.

nodes.label: Filter cards by text
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to type a text in the filter box **so that** I see only the cards that match it.

**Steps**
1. In the board toolbar click the box with the placeholder "Filter cards..." and type.
2. Press Escape or click the x button ("Clear filter") to remove the text.

**Expected**: The card list narrows as you type, in both views, and the card counter changes to "N of M cards".

**Preconditions**: A board with cards.

nodes.label: Match case when filtering cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to make text filtering case-sensitive **so that** "create" does not match "Create".

**Steps**
1. Click the "Aa" button ("Match Case [Alt+C]") next to the filter box, or press Alt+C while typing in the filter box.

**Expected**: The button turns active and only cards whose text matches the exact letter case remain.

**Preconditions**: Filter box in use.

nodes.label: Match any word when filtering cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to show cards matching any of my selected filters **so that** I get an inclusive search.

**Steps**
1. Click the "~" button ("Any Match [Alt+V]") next to the filter box, or press Alt+V while typing in the filter box.

**Expected**: The button turns active; with several members or labels selected, cards having at least one of them are shown. With it off, a card must have all of them.

**Preconditions**: Filters selected.

nodes.label: Filter cards by member
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to filter cards by members **so that** I see what specific people are working on.

**Steps**
1. In the toolbar click the person icon ("Filter By Members").
2. Select one or more members in the popup.
3. Click a member avatar in the toolbar, or the x "Clear filter" button, to remove it.

**Expected**: Selected members appear next to the icon and only cards assigned to them are shown (all of them, or any one if Any Match is on). Former members are flagged "This user is no longer a board member!".

**Preconditions**: A board with members.

nodes.label: Filter cards by label
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to filter cards by labels **so that** I see one category of work.

**Steps**
1. In the toolbar click the tag icon ("Filter By Labels").
2. Select labels in the popup.
3. Click a label chip, or the x "Clear filter" button, to remove it.

**Expected**: Selected labels appear next to the icon and only cards with them are shown (all, or any one if Any Match is on).

**Preconditions**: A board with labels.

nodes.label: Filter cards by due date
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to filter cards by a due date **so that** I see what is due up to a given day.

**Steps**
1. In the toolbar click the calendar icon ("Filter by Due Date").
2. Type a date or pick one in the calendar and press Save (Enter also saves).
3. To remove it click "Remove" in the popup or the x button next to the date.

**Expected**: The chosen date shows in the toolbar button and cards due before that date are shown.

**Preconditions**: A board with due dates.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say task due dates are always included; the app has a separate "Include Task Due Dates" checkbox in the popup.

nodes.label: Show cards for only the selected due day
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to show cards for one exact due day only **so that** I see just that day, not everything earlier.

**Steps**
1. Open the calendar icon ("Filter by Due Date") and choose a date.
2. Tick "Show Cards Just For Selected Day".
3. Click Save.

**Expected**: Only cards due on that exact day are shown instead of all cards due before it.

**Preconditions**: A due-date filter is being set.

nodes.label: Filter cards by notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to show only the cards that have notifications **so that** I can catch up on what changed.

**Steps**
1. Click the bell icon ("Filter by Notifications") in the toolbar filters.
2. Click it again to turn it off.

**Expected**: The bell button turns active and only cards with unread notifications remain.

**Preconditions**: Cards with notifications.

**Docs vs app**: Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Clear the card filter
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to clear a card filter with one click **so that** I do not have to deselect each item.

**Steps**
1. Next to the member, label or due-date filter click the small x ("Clear filter"). For text, use the x in the "Filter cards..." box.

**Expected**: That filter is removed and the hidden cards come back.

**Preconditions**: A filter is active.

**Docs vs app**: Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: See the number of cards after filtering
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see how many cards the filter leaves **so that** I know how much matches.

**Steps**
1. Apply any filter or text.
2. Look at the card counter in the toolbar next to the board name.

**Expected**: Without a filter it reads "N cards"; with one it reads "X of N cards". Each list header shows its own count the same way.

**Preconditions**: A board with cards.

nodes.label: Toggle filter options with keyboard shortcuts
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to toggle filter options from the keyboard **so that** I do not need the mouse.

**Steps**
1. Click into the "Filter cards..." box.
2. Press Alt+C for Match Case or Alt+V for Any Match; Enter applies and Escape clears the text.

**Expected**: The matching toggle buttons switch on or off without losing focus.

**Preconditions**: Focus in the filter box.

nodes.label: See which list a card belongs to in list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see which list each card belongs to in list view **so that** I keep my bearings without the columns.

**Steps**
1. Open list view.
2. Read the "List" column.

**Expected**: Each row shows the name of its list. Sorting by this column does not change list order on the board.

**Preconditions**: List view.

nodes.label: Move a card between lists from the List column
nodes.description:
**As a** editor, **I want** to change a card's list from the List column **so that** I can move cards without dragging.

**Steps**
1. In list view click the list name in the "List" cell of the card.
2. Pick another list of this board from the searchable dropdown.

**Expected**: The card moves to the chosen list (visible in board view) and the cell shows the new name.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Add a list from list view
nodes.description:
**As a** editor, **I want** to add a list from list view **so that** I can create stages without switching views.

**Steps**
1. In list view click "Add List" in the bottom pane (plus icon).
2. Enter a name and confirm.

**Expected**: The new list is created and also appears in board view and in the Add Card list dropdown.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Open a card from list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to open a card from its row **so that** I can see its details.

**Steps**
1. Click an empty spot of the card row. Cells for description, attachments and comments do not open a popup, so clicking them is the safe way.

**Expected**: The card detail modal opens over the list view, the row is highlighted, and closing returns to list view.

**Preconditions**: List view with cards.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say clicking description/attachment/comment cells opens the card; the app marks name, labels, members, list, due date, timer and tasks cells as editable in place (click does not open the card).

nodes.label: Edit a card inline in list view
nodes.description:
**As a** editor, **I want** to edit a card name directly in its row **so that** I can rename quickly.

**Steps**
1. In list view click the name cell, or open the card ellipsis ("Edit Card") menu and choose rename.
2. Type the new name ("Enter card name...").
3. Press Enter or click away to save; Escape cancels.

**Expected**: The name is updated without opening the card; an empty or unchanged name is ignored. Labels, members, list, due date, timer and tasks are also editable in their cells.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Sort list view by column
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to sort the table by a column **so that** I can order cards by what matters.

**Steps**
1. In list view click a column header.
2. Click again to flip the order, a third time to remove it.

**Expected**: Rows sort with an arrow in the header. Columns like attachments, comments, tasks, timer and notifications sort descending first.

**Preconditions**: List view.

nodes.label: Sort list view by multiple columns
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to sort by several columns **so that** ties are broken by a second criterion.

**Steps**
1. Click one header, then click another header.

**Expected**: Each sorted column shows its priority number; e.g. labels ascending, then name descending. Hiding a sorted column removes it from the sort.

**Preconditions**: List view.

nodes.label: Show or hide list view columns
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to pick which columns show **so that** the table fits my workflow.

**Steps**
1. Click the cog ("Edit List View") in the bottom pane.
2. Choose "Select Columns" and tick or untick columns.

**Expected**: The table updates and the choice is saved in my preferences. Extra columns include cover image, created at/by, updated at/by, description.

**Preconditions**: List view.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say to use the ellipsis in the top-right corner of the list; the app puts the menu behind the cog in the bottom pane (and an actions cell in the header).

nodes.label: Resize list view columns
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to resize columns **so that** I can give room to what I read.

**Steps**
1. Drag the | separator at the edge of a column header ("Resize column").

**Expected**: The column width changes live.

**Preconditions**: List view.

nodes.label: Fit list view columns to content or screen
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to fit columns to content or screen **so that** nothing is cut off.

**Steps**
1. Click the cog ("Edit List View").
2. Choose "Adjust Columns to Fit Content" or "Adjust Columns to Fit Screen".

**Expected**: Widths are recalculated; the chosen mode is checked and remembered.

**Preconditions**: List view.

nodes.label: Reset list view sorting and columns
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to reset sorting and columns to defaults **so that** I can start over.

**Steps**
1. Click the cog ("Edit List View").
2. Choose "Reset Column Sorting" and/or "Reset Column Visibility".

**Expected**: Sorting is cleared; visible columns return to the default set (cover, created, updated and description hidden).

**Preconditions**: List view with changes.

nodes.label: Page through cards in list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to move between pages of cards **so that** a big board stays fast.

**Steps**
1. Use the bottom pane arrows (First, Previous, Next, Last Page) or type a number in the page box and press Enter.

**Expected**: The table shows the chosen page; the box shows "page / total". The page containing the open card is shown first.

**Preconditions**: List view with more cards than one page.

nodes.label: Choose cards per page in list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to choose how many cards are on a page **so that** I decide how much I scroll.

**Steps**
1. In the bottom pane open the dropdown and pick 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000 or all ("per page").

**Expected**: The table repaginates and the choice is saved in my preferences.

**Preconditions**: List view.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say default is 100; the default is not set in the code read (stored preference).

nodes.label: Choose the list view style
nodes.description:
**As a** user, **I want** to choose a compact or default list view **so that** I fit more rows on screen.

**Steps**
1. Open user settings and go to Preferences.
2. Set "List View Style" to "Default" or "Compact".

**Expected**: List view rows are denser in Compact.

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say "compact or bigger (default)"; the app options are "Default" and "Compact".

nodes.label: Create a list
source: list.md#Creating, editing and deleting the list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a new list to the board **so that** I can organise cards into stages.

**Steps**
1. On the board, click the "+" (Add List) button after the last list.
2. Type a name in the "Enter list name..." field.
3. Press Enter or click the green "Add List" button.

**Expected**: A new list appears at the end of the board and the add-list field stays open, ready for the next name.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say a new pop-up opens automatically for the next list; in the app the same field is cleared and refocused. Empty names are rejected (field shows an error).

nodes.label: Create multiple lists in a row
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to create several lists without reopening the form **so that** I can set up a board quickly.

**Steps**
1. Click the "+" (Add List) button.
2. Type a list name and press Enter (the tooltip on the button also mentions Shift+Enter / Shift+Add List).
3. Type the next name and press Enter again.
4. Press Esc or click "Cancel" when done.

**Expected**: Each name becomes a list in order; the field is cleared and refocused after each one until you cancel.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs. The tooltip advertises Shift+Enter, but ListAdd.jsx keeps the form open after plain Enter and does not check Shift.

nodes.label: Rename a list
source: list.md#Creating, editing and deleting the list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to change a list's name **so that** the list matches how the work is organised.

**Steps**
1. Click the list name in the list header, or click the vertical ellipsis (Edit List) on the list and choose "Edit Name".
2. Type the new name.
3. Press Enter (or click elsewhere) to confirm; press Esc to discard.

**Expected**: The list header shows the new name; an empty or unchanged name is ignored.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Delete a list
source: list.md#Creating, editing and deleting the list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to remove a list I no longer need **so that** the board stays tidy.

**Steps**
1. Click the ellipsis (Edit List) in the list header.
2. Choose "Delete List".
3. In the confirmation ("Are you sure you want to delete this list?") click "Delete list".

**Expected**: The list disappears from the board.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Check list activity
source: list.md#Creating, editing and deleting the list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see the history of a list **so that** I know who created or changed it and when.

**Steps**
1. Click the ellipsis (Edit List) in the list header.
2. Choose "Check Activity".

**Expected**: A popup titled "Activity for <list name>" shows created-by/at, last updated-by/at and fetched activity entries; a back arrow returns to the menu.

**Docs vs app**: Docs only mention creation and last update; the app also lists activity entries and can fetch more.

nodes.label: Reorder lists by dragging
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to drag a list to a different position on the board **so that** the stages are in the order I want.

**Steps**
1. Press and hold the list header (the name area).
2. Drag the list left or right to the new slot.
3. Release the mouse.

**Expected**: The list is dropped at the new position on the same board; other lists shift to make room.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board; list is saved (not still being created).

**Docs vs app**: A list cannot be moved to another board or project (docs).

nodes.label: Collapse or expand a list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to collapse a list I am not working on **so that** the board is less cluttered.

**Steps**
1. Click the small triangle button ("Collapse List") left of the list name.
2. To bring it back click the triangle on the collapsed list ("Expand List").

**Expected**: The list shrinks to a narrow column showing its name and card count; expanding restores the cards.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board (the toggle is saved on the list).

**Docs vs app**: Docs call it hide/unhide; the app labels it Collapse List / Expand List.

nodes.label: See the card count on a collapsed list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see how many cards a collapsed list holds **so that** I do not need to expand it.

**Steps**
1. Collapse a list with the triangle button.
2. Look at the collapsed list column.

**Expected**: The collapsed column shows the list name and a count such as "3 cards" (or "2 of 5 cards" when a filter is active).

**Docs vs app**: Docs mention the count only in a screenshot; app code (cardsCountText in List.jsx) confirms it.

nodes.label: Mark a list as done
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to mark a whole list as done **so that** finished work is clearly separated.

**Steps**
1. Click the ellipsis (Edit List) in the list header.
2. Choose "Mark as Done" (or "Mark as Not Done" to undo).

**Expected**: The list is flagged completed; the menu entry toggles; completed lists can be hidden or shown via the "Hide Completed Lists" / "Show Completed Lists" option.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Email cards to a list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to get an email address for a list **so that** anyone can create cards in it by sending an email.

**Steps**
1. Click the ellipsis (Edit List) in the list header.
2. Choose "Email Card to List" (shows a count of addresses).
3. Click "Generate New Email" (clipboard icon "Copy Email" copies it; "Reset Email" regenerates; "Delete Email" removes it).

**Expected**: A generated address is listed; filter the list with "Filter emails by user...". The tooltip explains the subject syntax (card name, @user, #label, !due date) and body (description, attachments, task lists).

**Preconditions**: Edit rights and the instance mail service available; otherwise the entry is disabled with "Email service is unavailable. Contact 4ga Boards instance admin."

**Docs vs app**: Not in the user docs list page; see dev/notifications.md for Email-to-Card.

nodes.label: Create a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a card to a list **so that** I can track a new piece of work.

**Steps**
1. At the bottom of a list click "+ Add Card" (or the "+" button on a collapsed list).
2. Type the card title in "Enter card name... [Ctrl+Enter] - open".
3. Press Enter or click "Add Card".

**Expected**: A card with that title appears at the bottom of the list.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: In the app the inline field stays open after Enter so the next card can be typed; docs say Shift+Enter is needed for multiple cards (that holds for the Add Card popup).

nodes.label: Create a card from the list menu
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a card from the list menu **so that** the card lands where I expect.

**Steps**
1. Click the ellipsis (Edit List) in the list header.
2. Choose "Add Card".
3. Type the title and press Enter.

**Expected**: The add-card field opens in the list and the new card is created.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say the card is created at the bottom of the list; the app opens the field at the top (List.jsx handleCardAdd sets addCardAtTop).

nodes.label: Create a card in a collapsed list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a card to a collapsed list **so that** I do not have to expand it first.

**Steps**
1. On the collapsed list click its "+" button (Add Card).
2. Type the title in the popup; the list is preselected.
3. Press Enter or click "Add Card".

**Expected**: The card is added to that list while it stays collapsed.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Create a card in list view
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a card while in list view **so that** I can create cards without the board.

**Steps**
1. Switch to list view.
2. Click "+ Add Card" in the bottom navigation pane.
3. Choose the list from the dropdown and type the title.
4. Press Enter or click "Add Card".

**Expected**: The card is added to the chosen list and appears in the table.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: If no list is chosen the list dropdown opens and shows an error.

nodes.label: Create a card and open it
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to create a card and open it straight away **so that** I can fill in details immediately.

**Steps**
1. Start adding a card and type the title.
2. Press Ctrl+Enter (or Ctrl + click "Add Card").

**Expected**: The card is created and its card view opens on the right.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Create multiple cards in a row
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to create several cards in a row **so that** I can capture a batch of tasks quickly.

**Steps**
1. Open the add-card field (in the Add Card popup hold Shift).
2. Type a title and press Shift+Enter (or Shift + click "Add Card").
3. Repeat for each card.

**Expected**: Each card is created and the field is cleared and kept open for the next one.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: In the inline list field plain Enter already keeps it open.

nodes.label: Cancel creating a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to abort creating a card **so that** no empty card is left behind.

**Steps**
1. While the add-card field is open press Esc or click "Cancel".
2. Alternatively click an empty spot on the board (only works while the title is empty).

**Expected**: The field closes and no card is created.

**Preconditions**: Add-card field open.

**Docs vs app**: Docs: clicking elsewhere only cancels an empty title; the app closes on blur only when the title is empty (consistent).

nodes.label: Create a card by email
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to create a card by sending an email **so that** I can add work from my inbox.

**Steps**
1. Open a list's ellipsis menu and choose "Email Card to List" (or the board equivalent "Email Card to Board").
2. Click "Generate New Email" and copy the address with "Copy Email".
3. Send an email to it: subject = card name (may add @user, #label, !2027-12-31); body = description, attachments, task lists like "- [ ] Task 1".

**Expected**: A card appears in the list/board with the title, assignee, label, due date, description and tasks taken from the email.

**Preconditions**: Mail service enabled on the instance (see dev/notifications.md); sender is allowed.

nodes.label: Move a card between lists by dragging
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to drag a card to another list **so that** I can move work through the stages.

**Steps**
1. Press and hold a card.
2. Drag it to the target position in the same or another list on this board.
3. Release.

**Expected**: The card is placed at the dropped position.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

**Docs vs app**: Dragging only works within the current board; use the card menu to move it to another board or project.

nodes.label: Drop a card into a collapsed list
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to drop a card onto a collapsed list **so that** I can file work without expanding it.

**Steps**
1. Drag a card over a collapsed list; a gap shows which list receives it.
2. Release.

**Expected**: The card is stored at the bottom of that collapsed list and the count increases.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Move a card to another list, board or project
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to move a card to another list, board or project **so that** it ends up where it belongs.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Move Card".
3. Pick Project, Board and List in the dropdowns.
4. Click "Move".

**Expected**: The card leaves its current list and appears in the chosen list (possibly in a different board or project).

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; target board and list exist.

**Docs vs app**: The card menu is the only way to change board or project (docs).

nodes.label: Move a card from the card view list selector
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to change a card's list from the card view **so that** I do not need the board.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Click the list name right below the title (triangle icon "Move Card To List").
3. Choose the target list in the searchable dropdown.

**Expected**: The card moves to that list.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; card view open.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say the card goes to the top of the target list; not verified in the client code (move request is sent by list id only).

nodes.label: Delete a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to delete a card **so that** obsolete work is removed.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Delete Card" (in the card view you can also click the bin icon).
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this card?" with "Delete card".

**Expected**: The card is removed from the list.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Rename a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to change a card's title **so that** it describes the work accurately.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Edit Name", type the new title and press Enter. (In the card view click the title instead.)

**Expected**: The card shows the new title.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Duplicate a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to duplicate a card **so that** I can reuse its content.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Duplicate Card".

**Expected**: An exact copy of the card appears directly below the original in the list.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights on the board.

nodes.label: Copy a card link
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to copy a link to a card **so that** I can share it with my team.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Copy Link".

**Expected**: The card URL is copied to the clipboard and the menu closes (no toast is shown in the code).

nodes.label: Check card activity
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see a card's history **so that** I know who changed it and when.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on).
2. Choose "Check Activity".

**Expected**: A popup "Activity for <card name>" shows creation, last update and recorded activity entries.

nodes.label: Open a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to open a card **so that** I can see and edit all its details.

**Steps**
1. Click a card on the board (or a row in list view).

**Expected**: The card view slides in at the right side next to the board, showing title, list, members, labels, due date, timer, description, tasks, attachments and comments.

nodes.label: Close a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to close the card view **so that** the board has full width again.

**Steps**
1. In the card view header click the X ("Close Card") button.

**Expected**: The card view closes; in list view the table returns to full width.

nodes.label: Rearrange lists and boards while a card is open
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to keep working on lists and boards while a card is open **so that** I can rearrange cards while writing a description.

**Steps**
1. Open a card.
2. Drag cards or lists, or switch boards in the board area still visible beside the card view.

**Expected**: The board stays interactive; the card view remains open.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Docs only; app code renders CardModalContainer inside Board next to the board view, which matches.

nodes.label: Show or hide card sections
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to hide parts of the card view **so that** the card is less cluttered.

**Steps**
1. Open a card.
2. Click the toggle ("Toggle Description / Tasks / Attachments / Comments") next to a section title.
3. Click it again to show the section.

**Expected**: The section is hidden or shown; the choice is saved in the user's preferences.

nodes.label: Subscribe to or unsubscribe from a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to subscribe to or unsubscribe from a card **so that** I am notified of new comments on it.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Click the bell icon at the top-left of the card view ("Subscribe" / "Unsubscribe").

**Expected**: The bell becomes filled (subscribed) or empty; while subscribed new comments raise a notification in the bell at the top-right.

nodes.label: Mark a card as done or not done
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to mark a card as done **so that** finished cards are obvious.

**Steps**
1. Hover the card and click the ellipsis (Edit Card) icon to open the card menu (or right-click the card if "Open context menu on right-click" is on). (or use the check icon in the card view header)
2. Choose "Mark as Done" (or "Mark as Not Done").

**Expected**: The card title is struck/checked with a Done icon; the menu entry toggles.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Open a card's actions with right-click
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to open the card menu with right-click **so that** it is quicker than hunting for the ellipsis.

**Steps**
1. Enable "Open context menu on right-click" in user Settings > Preferences.
2. Right-click a card (or list header or task).

**Expected**: The card actions menu opens instead of the browser menu; right-clicking links, inputs and text areas keeps the native menu.

**Preconditions**: Preference enabled.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Self-assign a card with the spacebar
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to assign myself to a card with one key **so that** I can claim work quickly.

**Steps**
1. Enable "Self-assign cards by pressing the spacebar key" in Settings > Preferences.
2. Hover a card (or the open card view) and press Space.
3. Press Space again to unassign.

**Expected**: You are added to / removed from the card's members. Space is ignored while typing, with modifier keys, or over an inner task.

**Preconditions**: Preference enabled; edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Assign a member to a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to assign members to a card **so that** everyone knows who does the work.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. In "Members" click the "+" (Add Member) button.
3. Tick the members in the list (search with "Search members...").

**Expected**: Selected members' avatars show on the card and in the card view.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; only members of the current board can be assigned (project managers add them in board options).

nodes.label: Remove a member from a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to remove a member from a card **so that** assignments stay accurate.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Click the members avatars (or "+" Add Member).
3. Untick the member (tick marks assigned ones).

**Expected**: The member is removed from the card.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Not described separately in the docs (the tick toggle is mentioned).

nodes.label: Add a label to a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to put labels on a card **so that** cards can be categorised and filtered.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. In "Labels" click "+" (Add Label).
3. Click a label name to select it (search with "Search labels or create one...").

**Expected**: The label shows on the card with its colour; selected labels are highlighted in the list.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; labels exist on the board.

nodes.label: Remove a label from a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to take a label off a card **so that** the card is no longer categorised that way.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Open the Labels popup via "+" or by clicking the labels.
3. Click the highlighted label again to deselect it.

**Expected**: The label disappears from the card but remains on the board.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Not separately in the docs (tick toggle).

nodes.label: Create a label
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to create a new label **so that** I can categorise with my own tags.

**Steps**
1. Open the Labels popup on a card.
2. Click the "+" button (Create new label).
3. Enter a name ("Enter label name...") and "Select Color".
4. Click "Create label".

**Expected**: The new label appears in the list and can be applied to cards.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Edit a label
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to change a label's name or colour **so that** existing cards pick up the change.

**Steps**
1. Open the Labels popup.
2. Click the pencil icon ("Edit Label") next to a label.
3. Change name and/or colour.
4. Click "Save".

**Expected**: The label updates everywhere it is used.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Delete a label
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to delete a label **so that** unused tags are gone.

**Steps**
1. Open the Labels popup and click the pencil icon next to the label.
2. Click "Delete".
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this label?" with "Delete label".

**Expected**: The label is removed from the board and all cards.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Set a card due date
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to give a card a due date **so that** deadlines are visible.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. In "Due Date" click "+" (Add Due Date).
3. Enter date ("Enter due date...") and time.
4. Click "Save".

**Expected**: The due date shows on the card and card view, coloured by urgency.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Edit or remove a card due date
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to change or remove a due date **so that** it stays correct.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
