2. Click the pencil ("Edit Due Date") or the date itself.
3. Change date/time and click "Save", or click "Remove".

**Expected**: The new date is shown, or the due date is cleared.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; card has a due date.

nodes.label: See due date urgency colors
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see due date urgency at a glance **so that** I know what is late or close.

**Steps**
1. Look at a card's due date badge on the board or in the card view.

**Expected**: The badge is grey when the date is more than two weeks away, yellow within two weeks, and red when overdue (a card marked completed is compared with its completion time).

**Preconditions**: Card has a due date.

nodes.label: See a card's closest due date
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see the closest due date of a card and its tasks **so that** I know the next deadline.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Look at the "Earliest Due" row.

**Expected**: The row shows the earliest due date among the card and its tasks; it can be hidden via "Hide Closest Due Date" in preferences.

**Preconditions**: Card or a task has a due date.

nodes.label: Start or stop a card timer
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to time how long a card takes **so that** I can track effort.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view. (or use the card on the board)
2. Click the timer in "Timer" to start; click again to stop ("Start Timer" / "Stop Timer").

**Expected**: A running timer is shown in green; stopping adds the elapsed time to the total.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Edit or reset a card timer
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to set or reset a card's time manually **so that** the total is correct.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. Click the pencil ("Edit Timer").
3. Enter Hours, Minutes, Seconds and click "Save", or click "Remove" to reset; "Start"/"Stop" is also available.

**Expected**: The timer shows the new total (or is cleared).

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Add a task to a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to add a task to a card **so that** I can break the work into steps.

**Steps**
1. Click the card to open the card view.
2. In "Tasks" click "+" (Add Task) or the "Add Task" button.
3. Type in "Enter task description..." and press Enter.

**Expected**: The task appears in the list with an unchecked box; adding stays open for the next.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Mark a task as done
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to tick a task off **so that** progress is visible.

**Steps**
1. In the Tasks section click the checkbox ("Mark as Done") left of the task.

**Expected**: The task text is crossed out and the progress bar advances.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Rename a task
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to edit a task's text **so that** it stays accurate.

**Steps**
1. Click the task text (or ellipsis > "Edit Description").
2. Change the text and press Enter or click "Save".

**Expected**: The task shows the new text.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Delete a task
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to delete a task **so that** obsolete steps are gone.

**Steps**
1. Hover the task and click the ellipsis ("Edit Task").
2. Choose "Delete Task".
3. Confirm "Are you sure you want to delete this task?".

**Expected**: The task disappears and progress is recalculated.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Duplicate a task
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to copy a task **so that** I can repeat similar steps.

**Steps**
1. Hover the task and click the ellipsis.
2. Choose "Duplicate Task".

**Expected**: A copy of the task appears.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Assign a member to a task
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to assign members to a task **so that** it is clear who does that step.

**Steps**
1. Click the task's ellipsis.
2. Choose "Add Members" (or "Edit Members" when some exist).
3. Tick members.

**Expected**: Avatars appear at the right of the task, in card view and on the board when tasks are expanded.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Set a task due date
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to give a task a due date **so that** step deadlines are visible.

**Steps**
1. Click the task's ellipsis.
2. Choose "Add Due Date" (or "Edit Due Date").
3. Enter date/time and "Save".

**Expected**: The date appears at the right of the task and feeds the card's earliest due date.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights.

nodes.label: Check task activity
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see the history of a task **so that** I know who changed it.

**Steps**
1. Click the task's ellipsis.
2. Choose "Check Activity".

**Expected**: A popup "Activity for <task>" shows its history.

**Docs vs app**: Docs list it; app TaskActionsPopup has the Activity step too.

nodes.label: Show or hide tasks on a card
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to show or hide a card's tasks on the board **so that** the board stays compact.

**Steps**
1. On a card on the board find the tasks progress bar.
2. Click the triangle icon ("Show Tasks" / "Hide Tasks").

**Expected**: The task list expands or collapses on the card; in the card view the section toggle does the same.

nodes.label: See task completion progress
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see how many tasks are done **so that** I can gauge progress.

**Steps**
1. Look at the thin progress bar under the card's tasks (board and card view).

**Expected**: The bar fills in proportion to completed tasks, red to green; empty when no tasks or none done.

**Preconditions**: Card has tasks.

nodes.label: Reorder tasks by dragging
nodes.description:
**As a** board member with edit rights, **I want** to reorder tasks **so that** the order matches priority.

**Steps**
1. Press and hold a task.
2. Drag it to a new position in the list.
3. Release.

**Expected**: The task keeps the new position.

**Preconditions**: Edit rights; task saved.

**Docs vs app**: Not in the docs.

nodes.label: Edit a card description
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to write a description on a card, **so that** the card carries the details of the task in formatted text.

**Steps**
1. Open the card (it opens as the card view on the right side of the screen).
2. In the **Description** section, click the pencil icon (title "Edit Description"), or the plus icon ("Add Description") if the card has none, or click the existing description text.
3. Type in the editor (placeholder "Enter description...").
4. Click **Save** (or press `Ctrl` + `Enter`). Click **Cancel** or press `Esc` to discard.

**Expected**: The editor closes and the description is shown as rendered markdown. If you click away with unsaved changes, the text is kept as a local draft and the editor reopens with it next time (see the unsaved-text indicator).

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card; users without edit rights only see the rendered description.

**Docs vs app**: card.md only mentions the description briefly under Card options; the Save/Cancel buttons and Esc come from the app code.

nodes.label: Show or hide a card description
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to hide or show the description in the card view, **so that** a cluttered card is easier to scan.

**Steps**
1. Open a card.
2. In the **Description** header click the `-` icon (title "Toggle Description") to hide the section content.
3. Click the `+` icon in the same place to show it again.

**Expected**: The description (and its editor) collapses or expands. The choice is saved as a personal preference, so it stays that way for other cards.

**Docs vs app**: card.md describes the same `-`/`+` toggle for description, tasks, attachments and comments, in the Card options intro.

nodes.label: Add an attachment to a card
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to attach files to a card, **so that** related documents and images stay with the task.

**Steps**
1. Open the card and go to the **Attachments** section.
2. Click the **Add Attachment** field ("(Drop here, Ctrl+V or click to upload)"), or the plus icon in the Attachments header ("Add Attachment").
3. Select one or more files from your disk in the file dialog.

**Expected**: Each file appears in the Attachments list with a spinner while uploading, then a thumbnail (images) or file extension, the file name and the creation date. The header shows the attachment count.

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Add an attachment by dropping or pasting a file
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to drop or paste a file onto a card, **so that** I can attach it without opening a file dialog.

**Steps**
1. Open the card.
2. Drag one or more files from your computer onto the card view (a "Drop files to upload" overlay appears), or copy a file and press `Ctrl` + `V`.
3. Release the files.

**Expected**: Each file is uploaded and added to the Attachments list.

**Docs vs app**: Both agree. The app also reacts to pasting plain text (see "Create a text file attachment"). Firefox does not provide multiple pasted files (noted in the code).

**Preconditions**: The card view is open and the user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Create a text file attachment
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to turn copied text into a .txt attachment, **so that** long snippets are stored as a file on the card.

**Steps**
1. Copy some text.
2. With the card view open (and no text field focused), press `Ctrl` + `V`.
3. In the "Create Text File" dialog, type a name in "Enter file name..." (the `.txt` suffix is added).
4. Click **Create file**.

**Expected**: A `<name>.txt` file containing the pasted text is added to the card's attachments. An empty name is rejected: the field is highlighted as an error.

**Docs vs app**: Not documented; app only.

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Rename an attachment
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to rename an attachment, **so that** its name says what it is.

**Steps**
1. In the card's **Attachments** list, find the attachment.
2. Click the pencil icon (title "Edit Attachment Name").
3. In the "Edit Attachment Name" popup, change the name ("Enter attachment name...").
4. Click **Save**.

**Expected**: The attachment shows the new name. An empty name is rejected (field shown as error); saving an unchanged name does nothing.

**Docs vs app**: Not documented; the docs only mention the pencil icon for deleting (see "Delete an attachment").

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Delete an attachment
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to delete an attachment, **so that** outdated or wrong files are removed from the card.

**Steps**
1. In the card's **Attachments** list, find the attachment.
2. Click the trash icon (title "Delete Attachment").
3. In the "Delete Attachment" popup ("Are you sure you want to delete this attachment?") click **Delete attachment**.

**Expected**: The attachment disappears from the list. If it was the card cover, the cover is gone as well.

**Docs vs app**: card.md says to hover the attachment, click the pencil icon and select "Delete attachment". In the app the pencil icon only edits the name, and a separate trash icon deletes.

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Download an attachment
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to download an attachment, **so that** I can open the file on my computer.

**Steps**
1. In the card's **Attachments** list, click the attachment's thumbnail. For a file that is neither an image nor a PDF the file URL opens in a new tab and the browser downloads it.
2. For an image or PDF, click the thumbnail to open the gallery viewer and use its download button.

**Expected**: The file is saved by the browser. The server sends non-image, non-PDF files with a download header and only serves them to board members or the project's managers; otherwise it answers "Attachment not found".

**Docs vs app**: Not documented; app only.

**Preconditions**: The user is a board member or a project manager.

nodes.label: Preview an attachment
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to preview an attachment without leaving the card, **so that** I can check an image or PDF quickly.

**Steps**
1. In the card's **Attachments** list, click the thumbnail of an image or a PDF.
2. In the viewer, zoom with the mouse wheel, move between attachments with the arrows, and close it.

**Expected**: A full-screen gallery shows the file with its name as caption and a download button. Other file types have no preview ("There is no preview available for this attachment") and open in a new tab instead.

**Docs vs app**: Not documented; app only.

nodes.label: Make an attachment the card cover
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to use an image attachment as the card's cover, **so that** the card shows a picture in the list and board view.

**Steps**
1. Open the card and find an image in **Attachments**.
2. Click the **Make Cover** button next to the image's details.

**Expected**: The image becomes the card cover shown in the list; its thumbnail gets a star badge and the button changes to **Remove Cover**.

**Preconditions**: The attachment is an image (only attachments with a thumbnail show the button) and the user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Remove a card cover
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit cards, **I want** to remove a card's cover, **so that** the card goes back to its plain look while keeping the file.

**Steps**
1. Open the card and find the image marked with a star in **Attachments**.
2. Click **Remove Cover**.

**Expected**: The cover disappears from the card and the star badge is removed; the image stays attached and the button reads **Make Cover** again.

**Preconditions**: The card has a cover and the user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Show all or fewer attachments
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to expand or shorten a long attachments list, **so that** the card view stays compact.

**Steps**
1. Open a card with more than four attachments; only the first four are listed.
2. Click **Show all attachments (N hidden)** below the list.
3. Click **Show fewer attachments** to collapse it again.

**Expected**: The list shows all attachments, or goes back to the first four.

**Docs vs app**: Not documented; app only.

nodes.label: Add a comment
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can comment, **I want** to add a comment to a card, **so that** the team can discuss it.

**Steps**
1. Open the card and go to **Comments**.
2. Click the **Add comment** button, or the plus icon in the Comments header.
3. Write in the editor ("Enter comment..."; markdown, same editor as the description).
4. Press `Ctrl` + `Enter` or click the add button to submit. `Esc` cancels.

**Expected**: The comment appears in the list with your avatar, name and date, and the comment count in the header goes up. Card subscribers get a notification.

**Preconditions**: The user can edit/comment on the card. An empty comment is not submitted.

nodes.label: Edit a comment
nodes.description:
**As a** comment author, **I want** to edit a comment, **so that** I can fix or extend what I wrote.

**Steps**
1. In **Comments**, hover your comment and click the pencil icon (title "Edit Comment").
2. Change the text in the editor.
3. Press `Ctrl` + `Enter` or save; `Esc` cancels.

**Expected**: The comment shows the new text and an "Edited" marker (hover shows the edit time).

**Preconditions**: You wrote the comment (or have rights to edit all comments) and can edit the card.

nodes.label: Delete a comment
nodes.description:
**As a** comment author, **I want** to delete a comment, **so that** wrong or obsolete remarks are removed.

**Steps**
1. In **Comments**, hover the comment and click the trash icon (title "Delete Comment").
2. In the popup ("Are you sure you want to delete this comment?") click **Delete Comment**.

**Expected**: The comment disappears from the list.

**Preconditions**: You wrote the comment (or have rights to edit all comments).

nodes.label: Copy a comment
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to copy a comment's text, **so that** I can reuse it elsewhere.

**Steps**
1. Right-click a comment in **Comments**.
2. Choose **Copy Comment** in the menu.

**Expected**: The raw comment text is placed on the clipboard and the menu closes. The same menu also offers Edit Comment, Check Activity and Delete Comment.

**Preconditions**: The personal setting "Open context menu on right-click" is on. Not documented in the docs.

nodes.label: Check activity from the comments section
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to see the history of a comment, **so that** I know who wrote and changed it and when.

**Steps**
1. In **Comments**, hover a comment and click the activity (waveform) icon, title "Check Activity".
2. Scroll the popup "Activity for the comment by <name>".

**Expected**: The popup lists "Created" and "Updated" with user and time, followed by the logged activities of that comment (more load as you scroll).

**Docs vs app**: card.md says to click the `waveform` symbol in the comments section; in the app the button sits on each comment, not in the section header.

nodes.label: Check a user's activity
nodes.description:
**As an** instance administrator, **I want** to see everything a user has done, **so that** I can audit their activity.

**Steps**
1. Open the instance settings, **Users** table.
2. Click the actions (ellipsis) button of the user's row.
3. Choose **Check Activity** (activity across projects and boards) or **Check User Account Activity** (account creation and information changes).

**Expected**: A popup titled "Activity for <user name>" shows the entries with Created/Updated times; it loads more on scroll.

**Docs vs app**: instance-settings.md describes the account activity and the activity log of the user; the app implements it through the shared Activity popup (ActivityPopup).

**Preconditions**: The user is an instance administrator.

nodes.label: Format text as bold, italic, strikethrough or colored
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to style text in a description or comment, **so that** important parts stand out.

**Steps**
1. In the text editor select the text.
2. Click the toolbar button or use the shortcut: Bold `Ctrl` + `B`, Italic `Ctrl` + `I`, Strikethrough `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `X`.
3. For color, click the paint-drip button ("Add colored text") and pick a color: black, grey, white, brown, red, purple, pink, green, lime, yellow, blue, cyan, orange. Or type `<!--red-->text<!--red-end-->`.

**Expected**: In preview the text is bold, italic, struck through or in the chosen color.

**Docs vs app**: Both agree; the color button is added by the app on top of the markdown editor library.

nodes.label: Insert headings, links, quotes, lists and tables
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to add headings, links, quotes, lists and tables, **so that** long text is structured.

**Steps**
1. In the editor use the toolbar or shortcuts: title `Ctrl` + `1`..`6` (or type `#`), horizontal bar `Ctrl` + `H`, link `Ctrl` + `L`, quote `Ctrl` + `Q`, unordered list `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `U`, ordered list `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `O`, checked list `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `C`, and the table button.
2. Fill in the inserted markdown.

**Expected**: The preview shows headings, links (opening in a new tab), blockquotes, bulleted, numbered or checkbox lists and tables.

**Docs vs app**: Shortcuts are listed in card.md; the toolbar itself comes from the editor library (@uiw/react-md-editor), so the exact set was not checked in the app source.

nodes.label: Insert a code block with syntax highlighting
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to insert code, **so that** snippets are readable.

**Steps**
1. In the editor press `Ctrl` + `J` for inline code or `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `J` for a code block (or use the toolbar).
2. After the opening ``` add tags: a language (```js), then `showLineNumbers`, then highlighted lines such as `{1, 3-4}`.

**Expected**: The preview shows the code with syntax highlighting, optional line numbers and highlighted lines, and a copy button.

nodes.label: Insert a hidden comment in text
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to leave a hidden note in the text, **so that** it is not shown to readers.

**Steps**
1. In the editor press `Ctrl` + `/` (or use the toolbar button), or type `<!-- note -->`.
2. Type the note inside.

**Expected**: The note is visible only while editing; the preview does not show it.

nodes.label: Insert an image into text
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to put an image in the text, **so that** screenshots or diagrams appear inline.

**Steps**
1. In the editor press `Ctrl` + `K` or click the image button.
2. Replace the inserted markdown image placeholder with the image URL and alt text.

**Expected**: The preview renders the image.

**Docs vs app**: The docs describe only the button and shortcut; the app inserts a markdown image link rather than uploading a file.

nodes.label: Open markdown help
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to open the markdown help, **so that** I can look up the syntax.

**Steps**
1. In the editor toolbar click the help button.

**Expected**: The markdown "basic syntax" site (markdownguide.org) opens.

nodes.label: Link GitHub issues, pull requests and commits
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to link GitHub issues, pull requests and commits in text, **so that** the card points at the code work.

**Steps**
1. In the editor click the issue button and enter a number, or type `#1` or `GH-1`.
2. For a fork use `samplefork#1`; for another repository use `user/repo#1`.
3. For a commit type its hash, `fork@hash` or `user/repo@hash`; or paste a GitHub link.

**Expected**: The preview shows links to the issue, pull request or commit.

**Preconditions**: Per the app code, the references are only turned into links when GitHub is connected for the board (a repository is configured); otherwise they stay plain text.

nodes.label: Mention a user
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to mention a user in text, **so that** they are named and linked.

**Steps**
1. In the editor type `@username`, for example `@RARgames`.

**Expected**: The preview shows the name as a link.

**Docs vs app**: The docs list "Add mention" as a feature. In the app source MDEditor has "TODO add mention" and no mention button or board-user lookup; the only mention support seen is the GitHub-style linking of @names, which depends on the GitHub connection.

nodes.label: Switch editor view between edit, live and preview
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to switch the editor between edit, live and preview views, **so that** I can see the rendered result while writing.

**Steps**
1. In the editor press `Ctrl` + `7` (Edit code), `Ctrl` + `8` (Live code) or `Ctrl` + `9` (Preview code), or use the view buttons in the toolbar.

**Expected**: The editor shows only the markdown source, source and live preview side by side, or only the rendered text. The app stores the chosen mode as a personal preference separately for descriptions and comments.

nodes.label: Toggle fullscreen editor
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to make the editor fullscreen, **so that** long text is easier to write.

**Steps**
1. In the editor press `Ctrl` + `0` or click the fullscreen button in the toolbar.
2. Press again to leave.

**Expected**: The editor fills the window; leaving returns it to the card view.

nodes.label: Resize the text editor box
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** to resize the editor box, **so that** I have room for long text.

**Steps**
1. In the bottom-right corner of the editor box find the three small dots.
2. Drag them with the mouse up or down.

**Expected**: The editor box gets taller or shorter. Its starting height follows the size of the existing description (between 200 and 650 px).

nodes.label: Use text editor keyboard shortcuts
nodes.description:
**As a** board member, **I want** keyboard shortcuts in the editor, **so that** I can format and save without the mouse.

**Steps**
1. Focus the editor (description or comment).
2. Use `Ctrl` + `Enter` to save/submit, `Esc` to cancel, and the formatting shortcuts (`Ctrl` + `B`, `I`, `Shift` + `X`, `H`, `1`..`6`, `L`, `Q`, `J`, `/`, `K`, `Shift` + `U`/`O`/`C`) and view shortcuts (`Ctrl` + `7`/`8`/`9`/`0`).

**Expected**: The action runs immediately. `Ctrl` + `Enter` also saves when editing a description, a comment or a task.

**Docs vs app**: shortcuts.md lists only `Ctrl` + `Enter`; the formatting shortcuts are in card.md. The app code itself handles `Ctrl` + `Enter` and `Esc`; the rest come from the editor library.

nodes.label: See unsaved local text changes
nodes.role: board member who can edit cards
nodes.description:
**As a** board member who can edit, **I want** to see when my description text is not saved yet, **so that** I do not lose changes.

**Steps**
1. Start editing a card description and type something.
2. Look at the **Description** header, or click out of the editor without saving.

**Expected**: A "Local changes" label appears next to the Description header (yellow in the docs). The draft is kept in the browser, and reopening the card reopens the editor with it. The label disappears after **Save** or **Cancel**.

**Docs vs app**: card.md says the yellow text shows the changes are not yet registered on the server; the app label reads "Local changes" and applies to the description only.

**Preconditions**: The user can edit the card.

nodes.label: Open the notifications panel
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to open the notifications panel from anywhere in the app, **so that** I can quickly scan what happened on the projects, boards and cards I follow.

**Steps**
1. Click the bell icon (tooltip "Notifications") in the top-right of the header.
2. Read the panel that opens; click anywhere on the board to close it.

**Expected**: A side panel titled "Notifications (unread/total)" lists notifications, each with a category label on the left (Project, Board, List, Card, Task, Comment), the user and time, a description of what happened, and links to the board and project. The bell shows a count badge when there are unread notifications. With no notifications the panel shows "No unread notifications".

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

**Docs vs app**: The docs say the panel closes by clicking the board; in the app it is a popup that also has its own close behaviour, and the badge count is not mentioned in the docs.

nodes.label: Open the Notification Center
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to open the full-screen Notification Center, **so that** I can examine all my notifications thoroughly instead of in a narrow side panel.

**Steps**
1. Click the bell icon in the header to open the notifications panel.
2. Click the icon to the left of the ellipsis icon (tooltip "Open Notification Center", a fullscreen icon).

**Expected**: The app navigates to the /notifications page, titled "Notifications", which shows the same filter box, the ellipsis "Notification Actions" menu and the full list of notifications at full width. The side panel closes.

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

nodes.label: Read a notification
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to read what a notification says and jump to the thing it is about, **so that** I can follow up on the activity.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel (bell icon) or the Notification Center.
2. Read the notification: the coloured category label on the left, the user and time, then the description of the action.
3. Click the board or project name shown on the notification (or a linked project/card/list name in the description) to go there.

**Expected**: Each notification shows the category label (e.g. CARD, BOARD), the author with avatar, date and time, board and project links, and a message such as "Added user X to this card" (long names are truncated). Clicking a link navigates to that project or board and closes the side panel. If the board or project no longer exists, the link is dimmed with the tooltip "No board available" / "No project available". Notifications from 4ga Boards itself show the "4GA BOARDS" label, a tag, a title and text (polls show answer buttons).

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

**Docs vs app**: The docs list only the fields; clicking links through to the board/project is app behaviour that the docs do not describe.

nodes.label: Mark notifications as read or unread
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to mark notifications as read or unread, **so that** I can track which ones I have dealt with.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel or the Notification Center.
2. On one notification, click the eye icon (tooltip "Mark as read") to mark it read, or the crossed-eye icon (tooltip "Mark as unread") to mark it unread again.
3. To change all at once, click the ellipsis icon ("Notification Actions") and choose "Mark All as Read" or "Mark All as Unread".

**Expected**: A read notification is dimmed and shows the crossed-eye icon; an unread one shows the eye icon. The unread count in the panel title "Notifications (unread/total)" and the badge on the bell update.

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

nodes.label: Delete notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to delete notifications I no longer need, **so that** my list stays short and relevant.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel or the Notification Center.
2. Click the bin icon (tooltip "Delete") on a notification to delete that one.
3. Or click the ellipsis icon ("Notification Actions") and choose "Delete All" to remove every notification, or "Delete All Read" to remove only the read ones.

**Expected**: The deleted notifications disappear from the list and the unread count and bell badge update. The action applies only to your own notifications.

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

nodes.label: Mark all, delete all or delete read notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to change or clear many notifications at once, **so that** I do not have to handle them one by one.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel (bell icon) or the Notification Center.
2. Click the ellipsis icon next to the title (tooltip "Notification Actions").
3. Choose one of "Mark All as Read", "Mark All as Unread", "Delete All" or "Delete All Read".

**Expected**: The menu closes and the chosen action is applied to all notifications ("Delete All Read" removes only the read ones). The counts in the title and on the bell badge update.

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

**Docs vs app**: The docs describe only "mark all as read/unread, delete all, delete only read" in the ellipsis menu; the app uses a vertical ellipsis and the four items above.

nodes.label: Filter notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to filter the notification list with a text box, **so that** I can quickly find the notifications I care about.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel or the Notification Center (the filter box appears at the top when there is at least one notification).
2. Type in the filter box.
3. Press Enter to apply, or Escape (or click the clear-filter x icon) to clear.

**Expected**: The list is narrowed as you type, and a counter such as "2 of 10 notifications" appears next to the box. Clearing the text restores the full list.

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

**Docs vs app**: The docs call the first filter type "All"; the app names it "Aggregated" (placeholder "Filter by Project/Board/User/Card/Text/Activity Type...").

nodes.label: Filter notifications by category or activity type
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose what the notification filter searches in, **so that** I can narrow by project, board, user, card, or text and activity type.

**Steps**
1. Open the notifications panel or the Notification Center.
2. Click the double-arrow switch icon next to the filter box (tooltip "Toggle notification filter: aggregated/project/board/user/card/text [Tab]"), or press Tab while typing, to cycle the filter type: Aggregated, Project, Board, User, Card, Text.
3. Type the search text, for example a project name, or a text or activity type such as "taskcreate".

**Expected**: The placeholder changes with the type ("Filter by Project...", "Filter by Board...", "Filter by User...", "Filter by Card...", "Filter by Text/Activity Type..."), and only notifications matching that field remain. Typing "taskcreate" in the Text type shows task creation notifications.

**Preconditions**: At least one notification exists.

**Docs vs app**: The docs list "All, Project, Board, User, Card, Text/type of activity"; the app calls "All" "Aggregated" and the button shows the initial letter of the current type.

nodes.label: View an element's activity log
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to check the activity log of an element, **so that** I can see when it was created and updated and everything that was done to it.

**Steps**
1. Open the ellipsis menu of an element (project, board, list, card, task, comment, attachment, or a user in the users settings).
2. Choose "Check Activity".

**Expected**: An Activity popup opens showing "Created" and "Updated" with the user and time, followed by the list of all activity on the element. For busy elements such as boards, scroll down through the list to the very first entry; more entries load as you scroll.

**Preconditions**: The element exists and has been saved (the attachment option is disabled until the attachment is persisted).

nodes.label: Choose notification types to receive
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose which types of notifications I receive in the app, **so that** I only see the kinds of activity I care about.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the header and choose "Profile and Settings", then open the "Preferences" tab.
2. In the "Notifications" group find the row "Notification Types" (description: "Select the types of notifications you want to receive.").
3. Tick or untick the checkboxes: Instance, User, Project, Board, List, Card, Task, Comment, Attachment.

**Expected**: The change is saved immediately and the row's current value lists the selected types. Only notifications of the selected types arrive in the notification panel.

**Preconditions**: Signed in. This setting is not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Receive email notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to receive notifications by email, **so that** I am informed even when I am not looking at the app.

**Steps**
1. Verify your email address by clicking the link received in the verification email.
2. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
3. In the "Email Notifications" group, turn on "Email Notifications Enabled" (description: "Enable or disable receiving email notifications.").

**Expected**: The setting shows Enabled and further rows appear (types, delivery mode, skip emails for read notifications). Email notifications are then sent to the verified address, following your per-user notification settings. The group header shows "(requires email verification)" while the email is unverified.

**Preconditions**: Verified email address; the instance must have email notifications set up (hosted by 4ga, or a self-hosted mail setup).

**Docs vs app**: The developer docs describe only the service and the server setup; the toggle and sub-settings are visible only in the app.

nodes.label: Choose the email notification delivery mode
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose how email notifications are delivered, **so that** I can get them right away, grouped, or both.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. With "Email Notifications Enabled" on, find the row "Email Notifications Delivery Mode" in the "Email Notifications" group.
3. Open the drop-down and choose "Instant", "Batched" or "Instant then Batched".

**Expected**: The chosen mode is saved and shown as the row's current value; emails are then delivered according to the mode.

**Preconditions**: Email notifications enabled and a verified email. Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Choose email notification types
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose which kinds of notifications are emailed to me, **so that** my inbox only gets what matters.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. With "Email Notifications Enabled" on, find the row "Email Notifications Types" (description: "Select the types of notifications you want to receive via email.").
3. Tick or untick Instance, User, Project, Board, List, Card, Task, Comment, Attachment.

**Expected**: The selection is saved and listed in the row's current value; emails are sent only for the selected types.

**Preconditions**: Email notifications enabled and a verified email. Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Skip emails for already-read notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** emails to be skipped for notifications I have already read in the app, **so that** I do not get duplicate emails.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. With "Email Notifications Enabled" on, toggle "Skip Emails for Read Notifications" (description: prevents sending email notifications if the notification was already read in the app before delivery).

**Expected**: The row shows Enabled or Disabled. When enabled, marking a notification as read before it is delivered stops the email for it.

**Preconditions**: Email notifications enabled and a verified email. Not described in the docs.

nodes.label: Auto-subscribe to my own cards
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to be subscribed automatically to cards I create, **so that** I get notifications about them without subscribing by hand.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. In the "Notifications" group, toggle "Subscribe to my own cards" (description: "Automatically subscribe to cards I create.").

**Expected**: The row shows Enabled or Disabled and the setting is saved at once. Cards you create afterwards are subscribed to automatically when enabled.

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

nodes.label: Auto-subscribe to new boards
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to be subscribed automatically to boards I join, **so that** I get their notifications without subscribing by hand.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. In the "Notifications" group, toggle "Subscribe to new boards" (description: "Automatically subscribe to boards I join.").

**Expected**: The row shows Enabled or Disabled and the setting is saved at once. Boards you join afterwards are subscribed to automatically when enabled.

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

nodes.label: Auto-subscribe to new projects
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to be subscribed automatically to projects I join, **so that** I get their notifications without subscribing by hand.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. In the "Notifications" group, toggle "Subscribe to new projects" (description: "Automatically subscribe to projects I join.").

**Expected**: The row shows Enabled or Disabled and the setting is saved at once. Projects you join afterwards are subscribed to automatically when enabled.

**Preconditions**: Signed in.

nodes.label: Auto-subscribe to instance and user notifications as admin
nodes.description:
**As an** admin, **I want** to be subscribed automatically to user and instance notifications, **so that** I am told about changes to other users and the whole instance.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. In the "Notifications" group, toggle "Subscribe to users notifications" (changes of other users' email or username) and/or "Subscribe to instance notifications" (instance-wide).

**Expected**: Each row shows Enabled or Disabled and is saved at once. The header Settings and Users buttons show badge counts for unread instance and user notifications.

**Preconditions**: Admin account; these two rows are not shown to other users.

**Docs vs app**: The docs list the two options as admin-only items; the app matches, with wording "Subscribe to users notifications" and "Subscribe to instance notifications".

nodes.label: Suppress system notifications
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to stop certain system notifications from 4ga Boards, **so that** I am not bothered by messages and polls I do not want.

**Steps**
1. Open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences".
2. In the "Notifications" group find "Suppressed System Notification Tags" (description: tags you do not want to receive, separated by commas, e.g. general, releases, security, other).
3. Type the tags, for example "general, releases", in the "Enter tags separated by commas..." box and submit.

**Expected**: The tags are saved and listed as the current value; system notifications carrying those tags are no longer created for you. On the instance level, an operator can disable system notifications altogether with the SYSTEM_NOTIFICATIONS_DISABLED environment variable; then regular notifications and polls stop, but admins still get important security update notifications.

**Preconditions**: Signed in. Instance-wide switch needs server configuration.

**Docs vs app**: The data-sharing page says "you can disable system notifications" without a UI path; in the app per-user suppression is by tag and the full disable is an environment variable.

nodes.label: Receive new version notices as admin
nodes.description:
**As an** admin, **I want** to be told when a new 4ga Boards version is released, **so that** I can keep the instance up to date.

**Steps**
1. Make sure the instance is registered for system notifications (enabled by default).
2. Open the notifications panel (bell icon) and look for a notification labelled "4GA BOARDS" with a tag and title about the release.
3. To stop these notices, open "Profile and Settings" then "Preferences" and add the tag (for example "releases") to "Suppressed System Notification Tags".

**Expected**: A system notification appears with the 4GA BOARDS label, the author "4ga Boards", a tag, a title and text, and you can mark it read or delete it like any other notification.

**Preconditions**: Admin account; instance registered and not started with SYSTEM_NOTIFICATIONS_DISABLED.

**Docs vs app**: The docs state the release notices are admin-only and can be disabled per admin in user preferences. The app has no setting named for releases; it offers only the generic "Suppressed System Notification Tags" box, and the available tag names are not listed in the app.

nodes.label: Open personal settings
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to open my personal settings from the dashboard **so that** I can change my profile and preferences.

**Steps**
1. In the header (top-right), click your avatar/name (button titled "Profile and Settings").
2. In the popup menu choose **Profile**, **Preferences**, **Account**, **Authentication** or **About** (administrators also see **Instance Settings** and **Users**; project managers inside a project also see **Project Settings**).
3. Alternatively click the cog icon (titled "Settings") in the header, which opens the settings area directly.

**Expected**: The settings page for the chosen section opens with the settings side panel on the left.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

Docs and app differ slightly: the docs say the cog is reached after clicking the profile photo/name, while in the app the cog is a separate header button next to the avatar and the avatar opens a menu of sections.

nodes.label: Navigate settings from the side panel
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to switch between settings sections using the side panel and hide or show it **so that** I can move around quickly and free screen space.

**Steps**
1. Open any settings page.
2. In the side panel under **Settings** click **Profile**, **Preferences**, **Account**, **Authentication** or **About** (administrators also get an **Instance Settings** group with **Users** and **Settings**).
3. To collapse the panel click the icon button next to the 4ga Boards logo (title "Hide Sidebar"); click it again (title "Show Sidebar") to bring it back.

**Expected**: The chosen section opens and its entry is highlighted in the panel; the panel slides away or returns when toggled. The panel is narrower if **Compact Sidebar** is enabled.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Choose the interface language
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose the interface language **so that** the app is shown in the language I read.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Language**.
3. Open the dropdown and pick a language (or type to search).

**Expected**: The app text switches to the selected language. The dropdown offers **Detect automatically** (default) plus each available language with its flag; it is searchable.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Choose a color theme
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose a color theme **so that** the app looks the way I prefer.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Theme**.
3. Open the **Theme** dropdown and pick a theme.

**Expected**: The whole app recolors immediately. Options are **Default**, **GitHub Dark** (beta), **Light** (beta) and **Custom** (beta).

**Preconditions**: signed in.

Docs and app differ: the docs list only default, "GitHub Dark" and custom; the app also offers Light (beta).

nodes.label: Create a custom theme
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to create a custom theme **so that** I can set the colors myself.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Custom Theme**.
3. Click **Go to Theme Editor** in that row (the current value reads "Customized"), then edit colors in the table.

**Expected**: The **Theme Editor** page (settings/preferences/theme) opens with a table of **Color Name** / **Value** rows. Clicking a value opens a color picker ("Select Color") and the app recolors as you change it. A preset dropdown and the button "Override Custom Theme with <theme> Theme" reset the colors to a built-in theme.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Choose a theme shape
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose a theme shape **so that** elements have square or rounded corners as I like.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Theme Shape**.
3. Click the **Default** or **Rounded** preview button.

**Expected**: The app switches immediately between square and rounded elements. Two preview buttons are shown, **Default** and **Rounded**, and the active one is highlighted.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Choose the font for descriptions and comments
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to choose the font for card descriptions and comments **so that** long text is readable in my preferred style.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Preferred Details Font**.
3. Open the dropdown and pick **Default** or **Monospace**.

**Expected**: Card descriptions and comments are shown in the chosen font (the list-view descriptions too).

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Use a compact sidebar
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to use a compact sidebar **so that** the sidebar is slim and leaves more room for lists.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Compact Sidebar**.
3. Click the toggle in the row (title "Toggle compact sidebar").

**Expected**: The settings and board sidebars become slimmer (enabled) or wider, useful for long project names (disabled). The current value reads Enabled or Disabled.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Hide card activity in the card view
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to hide the activity details in the card view **so that** the card view is less cluttered.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Hide Card Modal Activity**.
3. Click the toggle in the row.

**Expected**: In an open card the created and last-updated lines are no longer shown. The current value reads Enabled or Disabled.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Hide the closest due date in the card view
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to hide the closest due date in the card view **so that** the card view shows only what I need.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Hide Closest Due Date**.
3. Click the toggle in the row.

**Expected**: In an open card the closest/earliest due date summary (from its tasks) is no longer shown. The current value reads Enabled or Disabled.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Show full due dates
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to show full due dates **so that** I see date and time on cards, tasks and the list view without hovering.

**Steps**
1. Click your avatar in the top-right of the header (button titled "Profile and Settings"), then choose **Preferences** (or click **Preferences** in the settings side panel).
2. In the **General** group, find the row **Show Full Due Dates**.
3. Click the toggle in the row.

**Expected**: Due dates on cards, tasks and list-view cells show date and time; when disabled the full date is shown only in tooltips. Not mentioned in the docs (undocumented).

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: See the current and latest version
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to see the build version I run and the latest available version **so that** I know if the instance is up to date.

**Steps**
1. Open the header avatar menu and choose **About** (or click **About** in the settings side panel).
2. Read the lines **Version:** and **Latest version:**.

**Expected**: The 4ga Boards logo is shown with the current version; the latest version is fetched from the project's GitHub and shows "Fetching" first, or "Unable to fetch" if the request fails. A demo-mode notice appears on demo instances. The page also has an **Import Getting Started Project** button (docs mention it too).

**Preconditions**: signed in.

nodes.label: Open documentation, support and social links
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to open the documentation, support and social links **so that** I can find help and follow the project.

**Steps**
1. Open **About** in the settings.
2. Click a link: **Website**, **Docs**, **GitHub**, **X**, **YouTube**, **LinkedIn**, **Facebook**, **Privacy Policy** or **Terms of Service**; or click the **Support 4ga Boards Development** button.

**Expected**: The target opens as an external link. The Docs link points to the Polish docs when the interface language is Polish.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

The docs list these links under About; the app contains them in AboutSettings, so the feature exists in both although it was only recorded from the docs.

nodes.label: Donate to support the project
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to donate to the project **so that** its developers can spend more time improving it.

**Steps**
1. Open **About** in the settings.
2. Click **Support 4ga Boards Development**.
3. Complete the donation on the PayPal page that opens (the docs say you can include your email to later request a feature, which raises its priority).

**Expected**: A PayPal donation page opens in a new tab.

**Preconditions**: signed in.

Docs (donate.md) point to 4gaboards.com/contribute#donate; the app button goes directly to PayPal.

nodes.label: Use keyboard shortcuts
nodes.description:
**As a** member, **I want** to use keyboard shortcuts **so that** I can work faster.

**Steps**
1. Ctrl+Enter: while editing a card description, a comment or adding a task, press it to save; while adding a new card it creates the card and opens it.
2. Shift+Enter: while adding a card (or list) press it to create the item and keep the form open for the next one.
3. Shift+Scroll: hold Shift and scroll to move across the board horizontally.
4. Tab: while typing in the notifications or sidebar filter, press it to switch the filter type.

**Expected**: The action happens without clicking buttons. 

**Preconditions**: signed in; the matching form or filter is focused.

Docs and app differ: in the app, plain Enter already saves a new task and creates a card (Ctrl+Enter then also opens the card); Shift+Scroll is not coded in the app and relies on the browser.

nodes.label: Open instance settings
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to open the instance settings and users screens from the dashboard, **so that** I can manage login methods and users of the whole instance.

**Steps**
1. On the dashboard, click your profile photo/name in the top-right corner to open the profile menu.
2. Choose **Instance Settings** (instance options) or **Users** (user table); both are shown only to administrators. Alternatively click the **Users** icon in the header (tooltip "Settings: Users"), which sits next to the cog **Settings** icon.
3. To jump between settings pages use the settings sidebar (**Instance Settings > Users** and **Instance Settings > Settings**); hide or show it with the **Hide Sidebar** / **Show Sidebar** icon next to the 4ga Boards logo.

**Expected**: The Users table (/settings/users) or the instance options table (/settings/instance) opens; the sidebar highlights the active entry.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator. A non-admin who opens these pages sees "You are not authorized to edit instance users!" (or the instance-settings equivalent).

**Docs vs app**: The docs say the Users icon opens instance settings; in the app that icon opens the Users table, and the instance options are under **Instance Settings > Settings** in the sidebar or the profile menu.

nodes.label: View the users table
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to see a table of all users, **so that** I can review who has access to the instance.

**Steps**
1. Click the **Users** icon in the header (tooltip "Settings: Users") or choose **Users** in the profile menu / settings sidebar.
2. Read the table under the heading **Users (N)**. Default columns: avatar, **Name**, **Username**, **Email**, **Admin**, **Email Verification**, **Last login**, and the edit (pencil) column.
3. Click a column header to sort (extra header clicks combine sorts); use the paging buttons and the "per page" selector under the table.

**Expected**: One row per user with the count of users in the heading; sort indicators appear on sorted headers.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

**Docs vs app**: Docs list name, username, e-mail and last login; the app also shows avatar, Admin toggle and Email Verification by default.

nodes.label: Add a user
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to add a user manually, **so that** people can log in even when registration is disabled.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users** (header Users icon or settings sidebar).
2. Click the **Add User** button under the table (plus icon).
3. In the "Add User" popup fill in **Email**, **Password** (with strength bar), **Name** and optionally **Username** (optional).
4. Click **Add User**.

**Expected**: The popup closes and the new user appears as a row in the table and in the **Users (N)** count. Errors are shown in the popup for "Email already in use", "Username already in use" and "Weak password" with the offending field highlighted.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent: the docs require e-mail, password, name and optional username.

nodes.label: Edit another user's settings
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to edit another user's personal details, **so that** I can fix their account without knowing their current password.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users**.
2. Click the pencil icon (tooltip "Edit User") at the end of the user's row — or right-click the row if the right-click context menu preference is on.
3. In the popup choose **Edit Information** (name, phone, organization), **Edit Username**, **Edit Email** or **Edit Password**.
4. Enter the new value and save.

**Expected**: The table row shows the updated value. No current-password confirmation is requested when editing someone else (it is only requested for your own account).

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say admins can change "all of the personal settings" of a user; the app offers only information, username, email and password, not preferences, theme or avatar.

nodes.label: Delete a user
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to delete a user, **so that** accounts that should no longer have access are removed.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users** and click the pencil icon on the user's row.
2. Click **Delete User** in the popup (not shown for your own row).
3. Read "Are you sure you want to delete this user?" and click **Delete User** to confirm.

**Expected**: The popup closes and the user disappears from the table.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; cannot delete yourself; the server refuses deletion in demo mode.

**Docs vs app**: Not mentioned in the docs; app-only.

nodes.label: Grant administrator rights to a user
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to grant or revoke administrator rights for a user, **so that** trusted people can manage the instance.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users**.
2. In the **Admin** column, click the toggle on the user's row (tooltip "Toggle admin").

**Expected**: The toggle switches state and the user gains or loses access to Instance Settings and Users.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; the toggle is disabled on your own row and in demo mode. The **Admin** column must be visible.

**Docs vs app**: Docs describe "toggling the switch blue"; consistent with the app.

nodes.label: View a user's account activity
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to check a user's account activity, **so that** I can see when the account was created and last changed (for example after a password change).

**Steps**
1. Open **Users** and click the pencil icon on the user's row.
2. Click **Check User Account Activity**.

**Expected**: A popup titled "Activity for <name>" lists account events with creation and last-update time and who performed them. Use the **Created at/by** and **Updated at/by** columns for the same data in the table (hidden by default).

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

nodes.label: View a user's activity log across projects
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to view a user's activity log, **so that** I can see what they did in projects and boards.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users** and click the pencil icon on the user's row.
2. Click **Check Activity**.

**Expected**: A popup titled "Activity by <name> (excluding projects you're not a part of)" lists the user's actions; more load as you scroll.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say the log covers all actions across projects and boards; the app title says it excludes projects the viewing admin is not a member of.

nodes.label: Show or hide user table columns
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to show or hide columns of the users table, **so that** I can see extra information such as SSO emails or who created an account.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users**.
2. Click the **Edit List View** icon in the last column header (or next to the paging controls).
3. Choose **Select Columns** and tick or untick columns (e.g. Email Verification, SSO Google/GitHub/Microsoft/OIDC fields, Last login, Created at/by, Updated at/by); use **Select Default**, **Select All** or **Select None**.
4. Alternatively choose **Reset Column Visibility** in the same menu.

**Expected**: Columns appear or disappear at once; a sort on a column that gets hidden is dropped. The choice is remembered in your user preferences.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

nodes.label: Resize user table columns and fit table
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to resize the users table columns and fit the table, **so that** all the content or the whole table is readable.

**Steps**
1. Open **Users**.
2. Drag the `|` separator on the edge of a column header (tooltip "Resize column") to change its width.
3. Click the **Edit List View** icon and choose **Adjust Columns to Fit Content** or **Adjust Columns to Fit Screen** (a checkbox shows which mode is active). **Reset Column Sorting** is in the same menu.

**Expected**: Column widths change accordingly; the fit-screen choice is remembered in user preferences.

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator.

nodes.label: Choose the user settings style
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to choose a compact or default style for the Users settings table, **so that** more rows fit on screen or the table is easier to read.

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name, then **Preferences** (/settings/preferences).
2. In the General group find **Users Settings Style** ("Select the style of the users settings.").
3. Pick **Default** or **Compact** in the dropdown.

**Expected**: The Current Value column shows the choice and the Users table switches density.

**Preconditions**: None to change the preference; it only affects the Users table, which only administrators can open.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent; docs name it "Users Settings Style" with compact or bigger (default) options.

nodes.label: Allow or block user registration
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to allow or block all user registration, **so that** I keep control over who can sign up.

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **User Registration** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the toggle in the **Modify Settings** column (tooltip "Toggle user registration").

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Enable or disable all user registration methods. If you disable all registration methods, only admins will be able to create new users."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Docs say to turn it off to retain full control (users must then be added manually); the app also disables the Local and SSO rows while it is off.

nodes.label: Allow or block local registration
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to allow or block local registration, **so that** new users can register with e-mail and password (or cannot).

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **Local User Registration** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the toggle (tooltip "Toggle local user registration"); it is disabled while **User Registration** is off.

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Enable or disable local user registration. This registration method allows users to create an account with a username and password."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent.

nodes.label: Allow or block SSO registration
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to allow or block SSO registration, **so that** new users can register through an SSO provider (or cannot).

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **SSO User Registration** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the toggle (tooltip "Toggle sso user registration"); it is disabled while **User Registration** is off.

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Enable or disable SSO user registration. This registration method allows users to create an account using an external account e.g. Google Account."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent.

nodes.label: Restrict registration to allowed email domains
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to restrict registration to allowed email domains, **so that** only people with approved e-mail domains can register.

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **Allowed Registration Domains** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the field (placeholder "example.com;example.org"), type domains separated by semicolons and submit.

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Semicolon separated list of allowed email domains for user registration. Leave empty to allow any domain."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent. Invalid domains mark the field as an error and nothing is saved; Current Value shows "Any Domain" when the list is empty.

nodes.label: Allow all users or only admins to create projects
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to let all users or only admins create projects, **so that** either everyone can create personal projects or only admins can.

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **Project Creation For All Users** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the toggle (tooltip "Toggle project creation for all users").

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Enable or disable project creation for all users. If you disable project creation for all users, only admins will be able to create new projects."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent.

nodes.label: Sync user data and admin rights from SSO on sign-in
nodes.description:
**As a** administrator, **I want** to sync user data and admin rights from SSO on sign-in, **so that** profile data and admin rights follow the SSO provider.

**Steps**
1. Click your profile photo/name (top right), then **Instance Settings** — or click **Instance Settings > Settings** in the settings sidebar (route /settings/instance).
2. In the settings table find the row **Sync SSO Data on Authentication / Sync SSO Admin on Authentication** (columns: Instance Settings, Modify Settings, Current Value, Description).
3. Click the toggle of **Sync SSO Data on Authentication** for user data and/or **Sync SSO Admin on Authentication** for admin rights.

**Expected**: The **Current Value** column of that row shows **Enabled**/**Disabled** (or the domain list) to match the new state. App description of the row: "Enable or disable synchronization of user data from the SSO provider during authentication. Enable or disable synchronization of admin from the SSO provider during authentication. Enabling this option can automatically grant or revoke admin rights based on the SSO data."

**Preconditions**: Signed in as an administrator; non-admins see "You are not authorized to edit instance settings". In demo mode the control is disabled.

**Docs vs app**: Consistent. These are two separate rows/toggles in the app, one feature node in the graph.

nodes.label: Use professional hosting
nodes.description:
**As a** prospective user, **I want** to use 4ga Boards on professionally hosted infrastructure, **so that** I do not have to install or maintain anything.

**Steps**
1. Open the pricing page at 4gaboards.com/pricing and choose the plan that suits your needs.
2. Alternatively open 4gaboards.com/try to try 4ga Boards first.

**Expected**: A hosted 4ga Boards instance is available without any installation; hosted instances also have email notifications enabled out of the box.

nodes.label: Install with Docker Compose
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to install 4ga Boards with Docker Compose, **so that** I get a running instance with its database in a few commands.

**Steps**
1. Download `docker-compose.yml` (`curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RARgames/4gaBoards/main/docker-compose.yml -o docker-compose.yml`), or create it from the example.
2. In the `environment` sections, edit `BASE_URL` to your domain or IP, set `SECRET_KEY` to a random value (`openssl rand -hex 64`), and replace `notpassword` in `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` with a random database password.
3. Optionally configure Redis for upload rate limiting (see "Use Redis for upload rate limiting").
4. Run `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: 4ga Boards is served at http://localhost:3000 (compose maps host port 3000 to container port 1337). Log in with the default user. Default user `demo` / password `demo` (overridable, see "Override the default admin user").

**Preconditions**: Docker and Docker Compose installed.

nodes.label: Update a Docker install
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to update a Docker Compose install to the latest images, **so that** I get new versions without losing data.

**Steps**
1. Back up first (see "Back up an instance").
2. Run `docker compose pull`.
3. Run `docker compose stop`.
4. Run `docker compose up -d`.
5. Optionally remove unused images with `docker image prune -a -f`.

**Expected**: The containers restart on the newly pulled images and the instance keeps its data volumes.

**Preconditions**: A Docker Compose install and a fresh backup.

nodes.label: Uninstall a Docker install
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to remove a Docker Compose install, **so that** the containers (and optionally the data) are gone.

**Steps**
1. In the directory with `docker-compose.yml`, run `docker compose down` to remove the containers.
2. To also delete the data volumes, run `docker compose down -v` instead.

**Expected**: Containers and network are removed; with `-v` the volumes (database, attachments, avatars, background images, Redis data) are removed too.

**Preconditions**: A Docker Compose install.

nodes.label: Run Docker as a custom user
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to run the 4ga Boards container as a custom user, **so that** it works on platforms such as unraid with the right file ownership.

**Steps**
1. In `docker-compose.yml`, under the `4gaBoards` service `environment`, set `PUID: 99` and `PGID: 100`.
2. On the `4gaBoards` service set `user: "0:0"`.
3. Start with `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: The container starts as root and (per start.sh) remaps its node user to the given PUID/PGID and fixes ownership of /app, public and private directories, then runs as that user.

**Preconditions**: A Docker Compose install.

nodes.label: Use Redis for upload rate limiting
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to store upload rate limits in Redis, **so that** limits are shared and survive restarts.

**Steps**
1. In `docker-compose.yml`, under `4gaBoards` `environment`, set `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_STORE: redis`.
2. Set `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL: redis://:<password>@redis:6379/0`.
3. Replace `notredispassword` with a generated password (`openssl rand -hex 32`) in all 3 places: the `redis` service `command`, the `redis` service `healthcheck`, and `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL`.
4. Run `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: Upload rate limiting uses Redis instead of in-memory storage.

**Preconditions**: A Docker Compose install with the `redis` service.

**Docs vs app**: The default docker-compose.yml in the repository already ships with the redis service and these two variables set to redis; the docs present them as an opt-in step.

nodes.label: Install on Kubernetes
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to install 4ga Boards on Kubernetes with the Helm chart, **so that** I can run it on my cluster.

**Steps**
1. Start your Kubernetes provider (e.g. `minikube start`).
2. Clone the repository: `git clone https://github.com/RARgames/4gaBoards.git` (or only the `helm-chart` directory).
3. Switch to the `helm-chart` directory.
4. In `values.yaml`, `auth` and `env` sections: set `password` and `postgresPassword` to generated DB passwords, `BASE_URL` to your domain or IP, and `SECRET_KEY` to a random value.
5. Run `sudo helm install boards .`.

**Expected**: The chart deploys the app; default URL http://localhost:3000. Default user `demo` / password `demo` (overridable, see "Override the default admin user").

**Preconditions**: Kubernetes cluster, Helm.

**Docs vs app**: The docs command reads `minkube start` (typo for `minikube`). The chart service is ClusterIP port 1337, so the documented localhost:3000 needs port forwarding.

nodes.label: Uninstall from Kubernetes
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to remove the Helm release, **so that** the deployment is deleted from my cluster.

**Steps**
1. Run `sudo helm uninstall boards`.

**Expected**: The `boards` release and its Kubernetes resources are removed.

**Preconditions**: Installed Helm release named `boards`.

nodes.label: Port-forward a Kubernetes install
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to reach a Kubernetes install from my local machine, **so that** I can open it in a browser without an ingress.

**Steps**
1. Run `sudo -E kubectl port-forward svc/app-4gaboards 80:80`.
2. Open http://localhost in a browser.

**Expected**: Local port 80 is forwarded to the `app-4gaboards` service.

**Preconditions**: Installed Helm chart.

**Docs vs app**: The service name `app-4gaboards` matches the chart (fullnameOverride), but the chart exposes service port 1337, not 80, so `80:80` may not connect; 1337 would be the matching target port.

nodes.label: Install on TrueNAS
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to install 4ga Boards on TrueNAS Scale, **so that** I can run it on my NAS.

**Steps**
1. Clone the repository (or only the `helm-chart` directory) and switch to `helm-chart`.
2. In `values.yaml` `auth` and `env`: set `password`, `postgresPassword`, `BASE_URL` and `SECRET_KEY` (random, `openssl rand -hex 64`).
3. In `values.truenas.yaml` `env`: set `BASE_URL` to the node address.
4. Run `sudo helm install boards . --values values.yaml --values values.truenas.yaml --kubeconfig /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml`.

**Expected**: Values in values.truenas.yaml override values.yaml; default URL http://localhost:30001 (the chart sets nodePort 30001). Default user `demo` / password `demo` (overridable, see "Override the default admin user").

**Preconditions**: TrueNAS Scale with the Apps service running.

nodes.label: Uninstall from TrueNAS
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to remove a TrueNAS install, **so that** the release is deleted.

**Steps**
1. Run `sudo helm uninstall boards -n boards --kubeconfig /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml`.

**Expected**: The release is removed from the `boards` namespace.

**Preconditions**: Installed TrueNAS release.

nodes.label: Install manually
nodes.description:
