**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to install 4ga Boards manually from source with Node.js, **so that** I do not need Docker.

**Steps**
1. Create and enter a directory, e.g. `/var/www/4gaBoards`.
2. Clone the repo (`git clone ... .`), or a specific tag with `--branch v3.3.11`; the default branch is the unrecommended `beta-latest`. To update later, `git fetch --tags` and `git checkout <tag>`.
3. Run `pnpm i`, `pnpm packages:build`, `pnpm client:build`.
4. Copy the build: `cp -r client/build/. server/public` and `cp client/build/index.html server/views/index.ejs`.
5. `cp server/.env.sample server/.env` and edit it: `BASE_URL`, `SECRET_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` (`postgresql://<username>:<password>@<host>/<database_name>`); optionally `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_STORE=redis` and `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_REDIS_URL`.
6. Make sure the PostgreSQL database is created and running.
7. `cp start.sh server`, `cd server`, `chmod +x start.sh`, `./start.sh`.

**Expected**: The server starts at http://localhost:1337. Default user `demo` / password `demo` (overridable, see "Override the default admin user").

**Preconditions**: Node.js, pnpm, a running PostgreSQL database.

nodes.label: Uninstall a manual install
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to remove a manual install, **so that** it no longer runs or takes space.

**Steps**
1. Stop the 4ga Boards process.
2. Remove the files.

**Expected**: The instance is no longer running and its files are gone.

**Preconditions**: A manual install.

nodes.label: Set up PostgreSQL manually
nodes.description:
**As a** self-hoster, **I want** to install and prepare PostgreSQL for a manual install, **so that** the app has a database to connect to.

**Steps**
1. Install PostgreSQL: Ubuntu/Debian `sudo apt update` and `sudo apt install postgresql`; Rocky/RHEL/AlmaLinux `sudo dnf install postgresql-server` and `sudo postgresql-setup --initdb`.
2. Run `sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql`.
3. Run `sudo -u postgres psql`, then `CREATE USER username WITH PASSWORD 'password';` and `CREATE DATABASE boards OWNER username;`, then `\q`.
4. Set `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://username:password@localhost/boards` in `.env`.

**Expected**: PostgreSQL runs with a `boards` database and an owner user that 4ga Boards can connect to.

**Preconditions**: A Linux server with sudo.

nodes.label: Migrate PostgreSQL 16 to 18
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to move a Docker Compose install from PostgreSQL 16 to 18, **so that** I run the current database version without losing data.

**Steps**
1. Create a backup: `docker compose exec -T db bash -c 'PGPASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD pg_dumpall -c -U postgres' > backup.sql`; check with `head -50 backup.sql`.
2. Stop everything: `docker compose down`.
3. In `docker-compose.yml` rename the db volume (e.g. `db-data` to `db-data-18`), change the mount to `/var/lib/postgresql`, and change the image `postgres:16-alpine` to `postgres:18-alpine`.
4. Start only the database: `docker compose up -d db`.
5. Restore: `docker compose exec -T db bash -c 'PGPASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD psql -U postgres' < backup.sql`.
6. `docker compose down`, then `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: All users, boards, cards and attachments are available on PostgreSQL 18; verify before deleting the old volume.

**Preconditions**: Docker Compose install on PostgreSQL 16.

**Docs vs app**: The current docker-compose.yml in the repository already uses postgres:18-alpine and volume db-data-18.

nodes.label: Back up an instance
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to back up my instance, **so that** I can recover it later.

**Steps**
1. Open a shell in the directory containing `docker-compose.yml`.
2. Run `./boards-backup.sh`.

**Expected**: A file `4gaBoards-backup-<timestamp>.tgz` is created, containing postgres.sql (pg_dumpall), attachments, user-avatars and project-background-images.

**Preconditions**: Docker Compose install with the db container running.

nodes.label: Restore an instance
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to restore my instance from a backup, **so that** I get my data back.

**Steps**
1. In the directory containing `docker-compose.yml`, run `./boards-restore.sh 4gaBoards-backup.tgz` (any relative path works).
2. If the database password differs from docker-compose, set a new password in docker-compose and comment out the `ALTER ROLE postgres ... PASSWORD` line in postgres.sql inside the archive before restoring.

**Expected**: Database, attachments, avatars and background images are imported; the script ends with "Backup restored from <file>".

**Preconditions**: A backup .tgz and a running Docker Compose install.

nodes.label: Set up Google SSO
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to let users sign in with Google, **so that** they can log in without a local password.

**Steps**
1. Create a project on Google Cloud Console.
2. Create an OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret.
3. Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the instance config and restart.

**Expected**: The login page shows a "Continue with Google" button under "or".

**Preconditions**: Access to the identity provider console; instance variables set in the config file of your install method.

nodes.label: Set up GitHub SSO
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to let users sign in with GitHub, **so that** they can log in without a local password.

**Steps**
1. Create an OAuth App or GitHub App on GitHub.
2. Create the Client ID and Client Secret.
3. Set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` in the instance config and restart.

**Expected**: The login page shows a "Continue with GitHub" button under "or".

**Preconditions**: Access to the identity provider console; instance variables set in the config file of your install method.

nodes.label: Set up Microsoft SSO
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to let users sign in with Microsoft, **so that** they can log in without a local password.

**Steps**
1. Create an app on Azure Portal.
2. Create the OIDC Client ID and Client Secret.
3. Set `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` and `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` in the instance config and restart.

**Expected**: The login page shows a "Continue with Microsoft" button under "or".

**Preconditions**: Access to the identity provider console; instance variables set in the config file of your install method.

nodes.label: Set up generic OIDC SSO
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to let users sign in with a generic OIDC provider, **so that** they can log in without a local password.

**Steps**
1. Create an app on the OIDC provider and get its Client ID and Client Secret.
2. Set `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OIDC_ISSUER_URL` and `OIDC_STATE_SECRET` (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 64`) in the instance config.
3. Register the redirect URL of the instance with the provider, e.g. `https://instance.domain.com/auth/oidc/callback`.
4. Optionally set `OIDC_ENABLED_METHODS` (Google, Microsoft, GitHub) to show per-method buttons; restart.

**Expected**: The login page shows a "Continue with OIDC" button (or one "Continue with <method>" button per enabled method).

**Preconditions**: Access to the identity provider console; instance variables set in the config file of your install method.

nodes.label: Set up email notifications on a private instance
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to enable email notifications, email verification and Email-to-Card on a private instance, **so that** users get emails and can create cards by email.

**Steps**
1. Host a mail server (e.g. docker-mailserver) or buy an external one.
2. Set up DNS MX, reverse DNS, DKIM, DMARC and SPF records, SSL certificates, and firewall rules for ports such as 465, 993 and 25.
3. Prepare the mail server config (`postfix-accounts.cf`, `postfix-virtual.cf`, `sni.map`, dovecot, opendkim).
4. Provide scripts that answer `NOTIFICATIONS_HOST_URL/api/clients/self`, `/api/notifications/email-verification/request` and `/api/notifications/email`.
5. Set `NOTIFICATIONS_HOST_URL`, `NOTIFICATIONS_CLIENT_ID`, `NOTIFICATIONS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MAIL_SERVICE_INBOUND_EMAIL` and `INSTANCE_NAME` (all notification variables are required).

**Expected**: Verified users receive emails per their notification settings; mail sent to a list or board address creates a card.

**Preconditions**: Mail server, DNS control. The docs admit this process is not easy and files/automation are not yet released.

nodes.label: Expose the log directory to the host
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to expose the application log directory to the host, **so that** I can read and ship the logs.

**Steps**
1. In `docker-compose.yml`, add `./logs/:/app/logs/` under `services.4gaBoards.volumes` (host path on the left, container path on the right).
2. Run `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: A `logs` folder appears next to `docker-compose.yml` containing the app log (e.g. 4gaBoards.log). Not enabled by default.

**Preconditions**: Docker Compose install.

nodes.label: Rotate logs
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to rotate the 4ga Boards log automatically, **so that** the log does not grow without bound.

**Steps**
1. Create `/etc/logrotate.d/4gaBoards` with a block for `/path/to/4gaBoards/logs/4gaBoards.log` (daily, missingok, rotate 14, compress, delaycompress, notifempty, create 640 root adm, sharedscripts).
2. Replace the path with your actual logs location.
3. Restart the logrotate service.

**Expected**: The log is rotated daily, kept for 14 compressed copies.

**Preconditions**: Logs exposed to the host (see "Expose the log directory to the host").

nodes.label: Ban repeated failed logins with Fail2ban
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to ban IPs with repeated failed logins, **so that** brute-force attempts are blocked.

**Steps**
1. Create `/etc/fail2ban/filter.d/4gaBoards.conf` with `[Definition]`, a `failregex` matching "Invalid email or username"/"Invalid password!" lines ending in `(IP: <ADDR>)`, and an empty `ignoreregex`.
2. Create `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/4gaBoards.local` with `[4gaBoards]`, `enabled = true`, `port = http,https`, `filter = 4gaBoards`, your `logpath`, `maxretry = 5`, `bantime = 900`.
3. Restart fail2ban and check with `fail2ban-client status 4gaBoards`.

**Expected**: IPs with 5 failed logins are banned for 900 seconds.

**Preconditions**: Exposed log file (see "Expose the log directory to the host").

**Docs vs app**: Matches the app: server/api/controllers/access-tokens/create.js logs `Invalid email or username: "..."! (IP: ...)` and `Invalid password! (IP: ...)` at warn level, which is the default LOG_LEVEL.

nodes.label: Replace a file in the container
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to replace a file inside the container, e.g. the favicon, **so that** I can customize branding.

**Steps**
1. In `docker-compose.yml`, add a `volume` entry on the `4gaBoards` service such as `- /docker/4gaboards/instance/custom-favicon.ico:/app/public/favicon.ico`.
2. Run `docker compose up -d`.

**Expected**: The container serves your file in place of the original.

**Preconditions**: Docker Compose install.

nodes.label: Enable HyperDX integration
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to send telemetry to HyperDX, **so that** I can monitor my instance.

**Steps**
1. Set `HYPERDX_ENABLED=true` and `HYPERDX_API_KEY` in the instance variables.
2. Optionally set `HYPERDX_INSTANCE_NAME`, `HYPERDX_TRACE_PROPAGATION_TARGETS`, `OTEL_URL` and `OTEL_URL_FORMAT` (default `http/protobuf`).
3. Restart.

**Expected**: The instance reports to HyperDX using the configured name; disabled by default.

**Preconditions**: A HyperDX account.

**Docs vs app**: Matches the app: server/config/custom.js reads HYPERDX_ENABLED, HYPERDX_API_KEY, HYPERDX_INSTANCE_NAME and HYPERDX_TRACE_PROPAGATION_TARGETS.

nodes.label: Override the default admin user
nodes.description:
**As a** instance admin, **I want** to override the default admin user, **so that** the first admin is not demo/demo.

**Steps**
1. Before the first run, set `DEFAULT_ADMIN_USERNAME`, `DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `DEFAULT_ADMIN_NAME` and `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in the instance variables.
2. Start the instance.

**Expected**: The default admin is created with those values (defaults demo, demo@demo.demo, Demo Demo, demo); applied only on first run.

**Preconditions**: A fresh instance.

**Docs vs app**: Matches the app: server/db/seeds/default.js reads the same variables with the same defaults.
